221	## Detailed Design
222	
223	### Core Rules
224	
225	Rules are grouped by topic (A-H); ids are stable, not sequential within a group (CT-42 to CT-44 sit with the topic they belong to). Rule ids are `CT-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas); acceptance criteria `AC-CT-n` (Acceptance Criteria) and open questions `OQ-CT-n` (Open Questions). Each rule is stated as **Rule**, **Why**, **Source**. Where two specialist proposals differed and no earlier ruling decided it, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: ...)". Names that Web Map & Transit marks provisional (`web.view`, `web.state`, `transit_state`) are used with that mark carried (WM-36). `HOME_ID` := the `derelict_id` of the `web.view.nodes[]` entry whose `kind` is the home ship (the WM-3 roster `kind`); it is a derived label, never a constant and never registered (WM defines no such constant). Godot-specific mechanisms are not designed here: each is marked "-> ADR candidate" (ADRs (a)-(f) are listed at the end of the section), and anything the engine reference cannot source is marked NOT SOURCEABLE. **Engine reference coverage:** `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/rendering.md`, `VERSION.md` and `breaking-changes.md`; there is **no** `scripting.md` or `core.md`, and nothing on `ConfigFile`, `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode`, `Window` display-mode APIs, `Input.mouse_mode`, key-echo detection, focus-out notifications, font-importer flags or AccessKit property names; those are NOT SOURCEABLE and are routed to the ADRs below.
226	
227	#### A. What the layer is
228	
229	**CT-1. A meta layer, not a place.**
230	*Rule.* The chart table is one PIPE layer-3 `CanvasLayer` in the **root viewport**, opened by the `chart_table` input action (Esc / Start) from the `gameplay` context only (in the pod, on a derelict, in the home-ship). In `inspect_card` the same press is consumed by the Adapter: the card closes first, the context returns to `gameplay`, no event reaches this layer, no `request_pause` is made and no overlay opens, and a running channel is untouched (PC-2 context return table; AC-PCI-170); a second press, now in `gameplay`, opens the layer (TX-13 / TX-14, governed by CT-3). In `chat` (VS-B) the layer does not open *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*. It has no prop, no location, no lighting, no glow, no ambient, no occlusion and no camera jolt. It is scaled by the HUD scale `H` for the bitmap face and continuously for the reading face (PR-12).
231	*Why.* A prop would be a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and could lie; the meta layer is honest by definition (ART 7.0 row 3: "can a reading lie? never"). The chart must be reachable on a sortie, which a home-ship console could not be. An in-world "chart-table console" or ship schematic does not exist (IW-28, C4).
232	*Source.* PIPE:94-103 (PR-3); PC-2 (contexts and context return table); PCI:78; ART 7.0.
233	
234	**CT-2. Truth channel.**
235	*Rule.* Layer 3 is never wrapped by the Perception Filter or by Sanity. No gleam, glide, tremor or settle occurs on any chart, panel or menu element (ART 7.3: the three motion signatures are readings only, and nothing on this layer is a reading). The layer is pixel-identical at sanity stage 0 and at forced stage 3, apart from the world visible beneath the panel. It never carries Violet or Flesh (ART 4.6), and Alarm Red appears on no element, because the layer draws no failing instrument (HR-4: red is never text). The only motion on the layer is the filament drift (CT-13, CT-40), the ART 7.3 cut/fade band and the ART 7.3 bracket ease-out, and the linear hold bar (CT-22).
236	*Why.* P1; ART HR-6 names menu, pause and settings layers as anchors; PF:223 (row 9, TRUTH: the pass sits below every `CanvasLayer`); SN:1226 (TRUTH anchor).
237	*Source.* PIPE PR-3 / PR-10; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-4, HR-6. **Note.** The world frozen or running under the panel keeps whatever it showed, including a lie (CT-4, Player Fantasy "Under hallucination"); the panel does not.
238	
239	**CT-3. Surface architecture: panel first, stable order.**
240	*Rule.* `chart_table` opens the **panel**, a right-third plate over the world (ART 7.4). The panel has exactly four items in this fixed order: **Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit**. The order never changes with state. An item that cannot act is shown **disabled** (the disabled style of CT-VA-7: Hull Grey label and a dashed 1-px Hull Grey border, so it clears the 3:1 glyph floor by shape plus tone; it is no longer Graphite lit, which measured 2.8:1), never hidden *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Default focus on open is Resume (non-destructive). Chart (and any message plate) replaces the panel in a cut (a replacement is not an appearance, so it takes no fade), except under reduce flashing, where it uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band (`CHART_FADE_MS`, CT-13). A replacement that raises layer-3 coverage is a governed raise (the re-open governor below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. "Display & Comfort" opens its page inside the panel's column. The panel carries only item labels and the empty status-line slot that holds `FAILED` when a write fails (CT-17, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); every paragraph of copy lives on a full-bleed **message plate** on the chart-table register (CT-28).
241	*Why.* One entry point; the world stays visible under the panel as ART 7.4 specifies; the HUD (layer 2) stays visible and frozen behind the pause panel, except that an active warning mark is held ON solid (HUD HS-23; the HUD's rule, acknowledged here; the full-bleed chart covers layer 2 entirely); a stable order is a muscle-memory affordance and menu layers are anchors that must not shift (HR-6). The accepted cost is that the chart is two actions from a pause; CT-10 (a no-pick console press opens the chart) offsets it. A second `chart` action stays an Alpha playtest fallback owned by the Player Controller and is not designed here.
242	*Ruled (HR-13, ASK-CT-8, OQ-CT-15, OQ-CT-27): the re-open governor. A player-initiated toggle of a large plate counts toward the 3 Hz ceiling, and the layer and the kernel are rate-limited together, never the picture alone* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director ruling)*.
243	- **Coverage levels.** `c = 0` CLOSED; `c = 1` the panel family (`PANEL`, `SAVE_FAILED`, `DISPLAY_COMFORT` opened from the panel); `c = 2` any full-bleed in-session plate (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`). A **raise** is a transition that increases `c` (TX-13, TX-14, TX-16, TX-17, TX-18, TX-24, TX-25); a **lower** decreases it (TX-15, TX-19, TX-35). Boot-flow screens are not governed (no world is visible under them and they appear once per process).
244	- **Close and resume are never delayed.** Every lower takes effect on the press frame. In SOLO a close calls `request_resume` on that frame.
245	- **A raise that comes less than `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` after the most recent lower is queued** and applied the first presented frame at or after `t_last_lower + CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` on the layer's UI clock (CT-43). A raise with no lower in the preceding interval is applied at once (the first open after a quiet period is never delayed). A queued raise applies **as one unit**: the plate, the focus, and in SOLO the `request_pause` of a CLOSED-to-PANEL or CLOSED-to-CHART raise happen on the same frame, so the picture and the kernel state always match (a queued open leaves the layer CLOSED and the kernel `RUNNING`; it never leaves an opaque plate over a running sim, nor a paused sim with no plate).
246	- **The queue is latched, one slot, and cancellable.** The pressed intent is held even if the key is released before the interval ends; there is one slot (the latest desired raise replaces an earlier queued one); only a `cancel` press while a raise is queued **cancels** it (the layer stays at its current level and a CLOSED layer is never opened and never paused) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: **a repeat `chart_table` press while a raise is queued is idempotent** (the raise stays queued, the latch is unchanged, nothing else happens), because at the first-launch default the lag is 1,000 ms and a player who pauses within a second of resuming (Moment 2, an emergency action) presses Esc twice from impatience and must not end up unpaused. **Queued acknowledgement:** the queue gives an audio-only acknowledgement (a single cue, no visual element, so no flash risk) requested from Adaptive Audio (ASK-CT-20; the layer plays no sound itself, CT-29): the cue is `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (semantics in CT-29, test in AC-CT-138); until Audio ships its asset the queued press stays the "documented reason" of CT-GF-2(1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. **Panel item state while a raise is queued from the panel** (Chart accepted, or Save & Quit refused into `UI3_PLATE`, within the interval of the last lower): the panel stays shown unchanged, all four items stay enabled, the bracket stays on the accepted item, and a repeat accept is idempotent; `cancel` cancels the queued raise first (the panel stays), and a second `cancel` closes the panel. The queue is cleared by any `request_restore` (TX-27). A queued raise has no hold or fill running, so nothing destructive is pending.
247	- **Scope.** The governor applies to the panel open (TX-13), the console-press chart open (TX-18; this supersedes the earlier "never to the console-press entry"), Chart from the panel (TX-16, TX-17) and the message-plate raises (TX-24, TX-25). It never delays the irreversible console press itself: a console press with a valid pick submits `pod_hop` at once and is not a layer raise (CT-10).
248	- **Value and derivation.** `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` = `ceil(1000 / FLASH_MAX_PER_S)` = 334 ms (registry `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, locked; same derivation as the registry's 334 ms floor for lying-readout ticks). With raises at least that far from the preceding lower, a rolling 1-s window holds at most three raises and so at most six opposing layer transitions, which scores `F <= 3` under the registry `flash_count` (Pipeline PR-13, D.15: `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)`). **Under reduce flashing** the interval is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` = 1000 ms (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 500-1500), so at most one raise per rolling second and `F <= 2`; with the long end of the fade band this is the toggle's real work. **Because reduce flashing is ON at first launch (user ruling D79, CT-19), 1000 ms is the interval every new player meets until they turn the toggle off**; the 334 ms interval is what a player who opts out, or a returning player who switched it off, gets. This is the price of the safe direction and is a playtest observable (OQ-CT-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The HUD's held-ON warning mark (HUD HS-23) is already solid under reduce flashing, so a pause adds no mark edge there.
249	- **Metric, defined once.** This GDD does not define a flash metric. The ceiling is the Pipeline's registry `flash_count` evaluated over the layer-3 rectangle and the frame mean from a per-frame linear-luminance log (acceptance AC-CT-115), on a bright lamp-lit fixture and on a fixture with an active held-ON warning mark, with the HUD mark edges counted in the same capture. If that capture shows `F > 3` on the mark's grid cell at 334 ms, the interval rises (range 334-1000) before the story closes.
250	- **Accepted cost, stated plainly.** A re-open pressed within the interval of a close leaves the world running with no plate for up to 334 ms (1000 ms under reduce flashing). This is the price of keeping picture and kernel together; the alternative of an immediate kernel pause with a coalesced picture was rejected because it can leave an opaque plate over a running sim or a paused sim with no plate (CT-GF-2 "Answered"). The PauseGate-deferred-resume alternative is **not adopted**: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the ruled form (layer and kernel rate-limited together, a close never delayed, a re-open queued and applied with its pause) stands (OQ-CT-28, D78) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
251	*Source.* ART 7.4, HR-6, HR-13; PCI:78; Pipeline PR-13, registry `flash_count` and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`.
252	
253	**CT-4. PauseGate (answers KRN Open Question 6).**
254	*Rule.* One adapter, `PauseGate`, with two modes. **SOLO (MVP):** opening the layer calls `request_pause`; closing it calls `request_resume` (KRN CR-15; PCI:147). **OVERLAY (VS-B, reserved):** no kernel call; the kernel stays `RUNNING`; panel and chart are identical. **No chart, pick, panel or menu rule may read `kernel.state == PAUSED`**; `PauseGate.mode` is the one place SOLO and OVERLAY differ. The single exception is inside `PauseGate` itself: it exposes one boolean, `can_save_quit`, true only when the mode is SOLO **and** the kernel reports `PAUSED` (Save/Load's `PAUSED -> SAVING`, SL-6, needs it); nothing else on the layer reads it except the Save & Quit item's enabled state. In OVERLAY `can_save_quit` is replaced by Session / Save-Load's form (`saveload.request_save`, reserved, SL:37, SL-17). Verbatim answer to KRN:961: **The Chart Table does not assume "pick a target" happens while paused.** The pick is a host-local selection valid with the kernel `RUNNING` or `PAUSED`; nothing depends on time standing still.
255	*Timing.* The layer enters PANEL on the press frame, or on the frame the re-open governor releases a queued raise (CT-3), whichever applies (presentation does not wait on the kernel); the kernel honours the control-plane request at the next boundary (CR-15, amended: the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service) and is `PAUSED` up to one tick later; the fade (`CHART_FADE_MS`, inside the ART 7.3 band) hides the gap, and `can_save_quit` is false until the kernel confirms. A same-boundary `request_pause` then `request_resume` (a double press) must leave no wedged half-open state: the layer keeps its own `open` boolean and `PauseGate` re-issues the latest desired state until the kernel matches (host-local, no commands). The kernel applies a same-boundary pair in arrival order, never coalesced, and ends `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle (CR-15 as amended 2026-10-27; ASK-CT-9 is answered), which is exactly the case the re-issue rule covers (a double press from a quiet start is an open then an immediate close; a double press within the governor interval after a close queues one raise and the second press is idempotent: nothing is sent until the interval ends, one `request_pause` then goes out with the plate, and only `cancel` clears the queue, CT-3, AC-CT-114c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to CT-3 and AC-CT-114c)*.
256	*Why.* KRN CR-16: pause is single-player only; in co-op a menu cannot stop a shared sim. Reading kernel state anywhere else is the divergence the brief's risk R4 warns about. The pause is available during a leg and during `TRANSIT_HOLD` and "changes nothing" there (WM:1268).
257	*Source.* KRN CR-15, CR-16, KRN:129, KRN:961; PCI:147; SL-6. **-> ADR candidate (a):** the relationship between kernel `PAUSED` and `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode` of layer 3 is NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference. Behavioural requirement stated here: layer 3 handles input and animates on its own UI clock (CT-43) while the kernel is `PAUSED`.
258	
259	**CT-5. Input depth: Esc closes, cancel steps back.**
260	*Rule.* In the `chart_table` context (PC-2 sends `set_move_intent {NONE}`, clears the run latch, **submits `cancel_channel`** for a hold-mode channel, and releases the cursor):
261	- `chart_table` (Esc / Start) is a toggle and **closes the whole layer from any depth** (SOLO then calls `request_resume`).
262	- A `chart_table` press made in `inspect_card` never reaches the layer (the Adapter closes the card, PC-2 context return table); every toggle rule in this section concerns a press in `gameplay` or inside the layer *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*.
263	- `cancel` (X / B) **steps back one level**: Display & Comfort, Chart or a message plate returns to the panel; the panel closes (PCI:73, "closes the current UI"). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:)* a chart opened by a console press has no panel behind it, so `cancel` returns it to `CLOSED` (TX-35); Display & Comfort opened from the main menu returns to the main menu (TX-37).
264	- **Hold exception (orchestrator ruling: the stricter, safer reading of the rulings).** While a hold-to-confirm fill is running (CT-22), release, `cancel` **or** `chart_table` aborts the fill (the bar snaps to empty in the same frame) and **nothing else happens in that press**; a second `chart_table` press then closes the layer. The alternative (Esc during a fill aborts and also closes) was proposed and declined: an Esc that resumes the simulation while a destructive hold was in progress is a second effect from one press.
265	- On boot-flow screens (notice, main menu, Display & Comfort opened from the menu, UI-5, UI-8, UI-9) `chart_table` does nothing **except abort a running hold fill (TX-10)**, and `cancel` goes back only where a previous boot screen exists (UI-5 to the main menu; UI-8 and UI-9 have none).
266	- During a Save & Quit write (CT-21, state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`) `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored so a half-written state is never abandoned.
267	- `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` are **not** actions of the `chart_table` context: the Controller emits the zoom edges from `gameplay` and `inspect_card` only (PC-2 context table; PCI source-scan criterion), so no zoom edge reaches the layer, and the wheel, `=` and `-` keys are not zoom here. No zoom row, hint or glyph appears on any surface (zoom is never a setting, PIPE:232). The mouse wheel scrolls in this context (legal across contexts); nothing scrolls at MVP *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "a zoom press is discarded by the layer" is stale; the D-pad is navigation, CT-45)*.
268	- **Directional navigation, accept, back and close come from the Adapter's MenuInput feed (CT-45)**, not from the layer reading devices: the four-way cardinal read, the deadzone hysteresis (`MOVE_DEADZONE` / `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, PCI, not registered), echo suppression and the latch on a closing control are the Adapter's. The per-device navigation set is stick, D-pad, arrow keys and WASD; accept is the physical controls of `interact` in this context (E, gamepad A, plus Enter and Space), **never a mouse button** (the Controller's `chart_table` note excludes every mouse button, PC-2a, ASK-CT-15 answered, C23 resolved) (a click is a `POINTER` event, CT-45) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*; back is `cancel` (X / B); close is `chart_table` (Esc / Start). The Controller's `chart_table`-context note (PCI default bindings) accepts the reuse of the `move_*` and `interact` physical controls and adds no action (ASK-CT-2 is answered for the reuse; the Enter and Space accept bindings and the LMB exclusion are in PC-2a). A rebind that removes the last path to the chart table on the active device is refused `BINDING_REQUIRED{chart_table}` by the Controller's side *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
269	*Source.* PCI:62, :73-80, :699; PIPE:688, 232.
270	
271	**CT-6. Focus is a shape; dual focus.**
272	*Rule.* Focus is the Tungsten bracket (left bar plus chamfer corners) **and** a one-art-px thickening of the focused bezel; never a Tungsten fill (ART 7.2, HR-11). The bracket relocates with a 100 ms ease-out (ART 7.3). The bracket is drawn from **keyboard / gamepad focus only**: it hides on mouse motion and is revealed again by the FIRST key or pad navigation press after that motion, which only reveals it on the retained focus and moves nothing; the next press navigates (CT-45 (c); PCI PC-13) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Mouse hover turns the item's label Tungsten (ART 7.4) and never moves the bracket; a chart node carries no label, so hover changes nothing on the node itself, the **pointer cursor changes shape over a selectable node only** (no art, no label; OQ-CT-9 closed) and the click's visible result is the route (CT-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A mouse click on an item activates it and moves key/pad focus to it, so the next pad press navigates from where the mouse acted; the bracket stays hidden until key or pad input. Glyphs follow the last device with `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` (PCI, registry; value in Tuning Knobs); mixed input is permitted. Every flow is gamepad-complete (HR-14). A click on an item is activated only when the pointer-up lands on the item that received the press.
273	*Why.* Godot 4.6 split mouse/touch focus from keyboard/gamepad focus (`modules/ui.md`, HIGH risk, "test with BOTH"): the bracket must be drawn from the keyboard/gamepad focus and not from hover or PC-13 cannot hold. Both paths are tested (Acceptance Criteria).
274	*Source.* ART 7.2, 7.3, 7.4; PCI:141 (PC-13); HR-11, HR-14; `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`.

276	#### B. The pick and the sortie
277	
278	**CT-7. The pick (`ChartPick`).**
279	*Rule.* `ChartPick` is NONE or one `derelict_id`. It is host-local presentation state of this layer: never simulation, never persisted, never a field of `web.state` or `web.view`, never assumed to depend on pause (WM-8, WM:1300). **Setting:** on the chart with `pod_at == HOME_ID` and `transit_state == IDLE`, accept (CT-5) on a legal target (CT-9) sets the pick, replacing any previous pick; accepting the already-picked node leaves it set (idempotent, so a double press cannot clear it by accident); accepting the HOME node (the origin) **clears** the pick; accepting a non-selectable node does nothing (**orchestrator ruling:** the ux-designer's rule; the ui-programmer's alternative, "accept on the picked node clears it, HOME is a no-op", was declined because a double press would clear the pick). Closing the chart or the layer **keeps** the pick. The pick is shown by a Tungsten dashed planned-sortie line from the HOME node to the picked node (WM:1048 "planned sortie"), plus the bracket wherever focus is: a shape difference (dashed versus absent), so no colour carries it. A focused but unpicked node shows the bracket only and never a previewed route (a previewed route is a recommendation by default). Nothing else changes on the node: no label, no number (CT-14).
280	*Why.* The pick is "the deliberate step" (WM:1225); the console press is the commitment (CT-10). Focus and pick are two states, so the player needs a non-colour way to see "picked" while the bracket sits elsewhere. The Tungsten dashed line **always means "the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight"** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `transit_state == IDLE` it is the target the next console press carries (HOME to `ChartPick` when the pod is at HOME, the pod's node to HOME when it is at a derelict); on an OUT leg, only in LEG and ARRIVING, it runs HOME to `web.view.leg_target_id` and confirms what the player committed to (CT-15; it never reads `ChartPick`); on a BACK leg, only in LEG and ARRIVING, it runs from `web.view.leg_origin_id` to HOME (the same line as the IDLE line from a derelict to HOME, CT-10), and it is **never** drawn in BERTHING *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G2)*. It is not a recommendation (from a derelict it is the only legal move; from HOME it appears only after the player's own pick), and this single definition closes OQ-CT-10 (the route is the pick mark; no second mark).
281	*Source.* WM-8 (WM:203), WM:1225, WM:1300.
282	
283	**CT-8. Pick lifecycle.**
284	*Rule.* `ChartPick := NONE` on: (1) any `request_restore`, for every `restore_reason` (`NEW_GAME`, `LOAD_GAME`, `DEATH_STUB`, `FAULT_RECOVERY`; SL-21); (2) arrival (`POD_ARRIVED`, WM-31), detected equivalently as `pod_at` leaving `IN_FLIGHT` so a test double needs no event bus; (3) whenever the picked record leaves the legal-target mirror (ABSORBED, ORPHAN, `berthed`, or absent from `web.view`). The pick is revalidated against `web.view` on every chart open and every `web.view` change. It is **frozen** (not editable) while `transit_state != IDLE`. No rule reads it except the console seam (CT-10). If the node holding key/pad focus leaves the selectable set, focus moves to HOME; the bracket otherwise does not move and no message is shown.
285	*Why.* A stale pick is the only way the chart and the press can disagree. The sim still validates with Web Map & Transit's own reasons (`TARGET_UNKNOWN`, `TARGET_ABSORBED`, `TARGET_BERTHED`, `BERTH_PENDING`; WM-9), which this GDD cites and never re-lists as its own.
286	*Source.* WM-9 (WM:205-217), WM-31; SL-21.
287	
288	**CT-9. Legal-target mirror.**
289	*Rule.* The chart computes `legal_targets` (D.4) purely from `web.view`, for **selectability only**: from HOME, derelicts whose `status` is not ABSORBED or ORPHAN and that are not `berthed`, **and none at all while any record is `berthed` and not ABSORBED** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Web Map's E-36 refuses every hop with `BERTH_PENDING` or `TARGET_BERTHED` then, and `berthed` is already a `web.view` field the chart reads, so an offered choice that cannot succeed is not offered); from a derelict, only HOME; with `transit_state != IDLE` or `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT`, none. UNSEEN derelicts are selectable bare nodes (WM:1299; OQ-WM-4). ORPHAN is drawn but neither focusable nor selectable (WM:1046). The mirror is **not a validation and not a second copy of WM-9's reason order**; every refusal is Web Map & Transit's and Interaction's, shown as words on the register plate (not here). **The mirror never reflects `FUEL_LOW`, `BUSY`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` or `CAPACITY`**; those refusals are words at the console only (CT-35). `BERTH_PENDING` is reflected only as the empty set while a record is berthed (below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **The one berth-driven emptiness** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while a record is `berthed` and not ABSORBED, `legal_targets` is `{}` from HOME (a `web.view` read, not a copy of WM-9's reason order); the chart still opens from the panel, every node is non-focusable except HOME, and no route can be drawn; the words explaining why are Web Map's `BERTH_PENDING` words on the register plate at the console (CT-10 R6), not text on the chart (OQ-CT-3).
290	*Why.* WM-9 defines `TARGET_ABSORBED` (WM:217) as "a welded-in or orphaned record; the Chart Table never offers it", so that reason already covers ORPHAN, and WM:1046 draws ORPHAN not selectable; the mirror is what makes "never offers" true. Greying a node on low fuel would put a fuel meter on the truth layer, which is why the exclusion above is a named sentence (CT-35).
291	*Source.* WM-4 (WM:193); WM-9 (WM:205-217).
292	
293	**CT-10. The console seam: the only simulation write.**
294	*Rule.* The chart submits nothing. The **pod console press** (Interaction's CONSOLE subject, `tool_required` NONE) is the only simulation write and the only commitment (WM:1225, WM:1301): no "confirm sortie", no resume-and-hop gesture, no confirmation dialog anywhere on this layer. Resolution at the press, in the Input Adapter's seam:
295	1. **From a derelict:** HOME is implied (WM-4, WM-8: "from a derelict the press carries HOME implicitly"). If the chart is opened there it shows the bracket on HOME as the only focusable node, and the planned-sortie line from the pod's node to HOME is drawn from `pod_at` (not from `ChartPick`), because that is the only legal move; the selection cannot move to another node. This implied line carries the same single meaning as CT-7's dashed line (the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `transit_state == IDLE` it is the target the next console press carries; the in-flight route (either leg) is CT-15's; it is not a recommendation.
296	2. **From HOME with a valid pick:** the press submits `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` at the POD prompt, or `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` at the DOCK prompt (WM-21). Which of the two a press means is decided by **which prompt was pressed** (the verb-resolution table below), never by a mode of the chart.
297	3. **From HOME with no valid pick, at a prompt that needs a pick (`pod_hop`, `berth`):** the press **opens the chart** (host-local, no refusal, no simulation effect), **even when exactly one legal target exists**: an auto-implied hop from HOME would make the press both choice and commitment. Default focus on opening is the pod's own node (HOME), never a target, so focus is never a recommendation. In SOLO the open requests a pause as in CT-4 and is a governed raise (CT-3). **This rule applies only to `pod_hop` and `berth`; `unberth` takes no payload, never needs a pick and is never swallowed by it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
298	4. **Verb-resolution table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; keyed on the facts the Adapter can read at the press: `pod_at`, `transit_state`, whether a record is `berthed`, and `ChartPick`; the prompt is the Interaction subject that was pressed)*. Console preconditions that are Interaction's and Web Map's (in reach, lit, `console_ready`) are evaluated first and answered in words on the register plate; the table starts after them.
299	
300	| Row | `pod_at` | `transit_state` | `berthed` record | `ChartPick` | Prompt pressed | Result of the press |
301	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
302	| R1 | a derelict | IDLE | n/a (berth starts only from HOME) | not read | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := HOME_ID}` (HOME is implied, WM-4, WM-8) |
303	| R1b *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a derelict | IDLE | n/a | not read | DOCK | **no DOCK prompt exists there** (WM-21: `berth` starts only from HOME; the DOCK subject exists in the home airlock only, IA-40; no DOCK subject exists at a derelict dock); through a test double Web Map answers `NOT_DOCKED_HERE` and the press submits no command and opens no chart *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
304	| R2 | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` |
305	| R3 | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | POD | opens the chart (entry origin `CONSOLE`, TX-18); no command |
306	| R4a | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | DOCK | `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` |
307	| R4b | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | DOCK | opens the chart (as R3) |
308	| R5 | HOME | IDLE | a record B | **not read** | DOCK | `unberth{}` (no payload; the DOCK prompt's verb is `unberth` while a record is berthed; never opens the chart) |
309	| R6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | HOME | IDLE | a record B (not ABSORBED) | not read (`legal_targets` is `{}`, so a pick is always invalid) | POD | **no chart opens and no `pod_hop{target}` is built from the pick**; the press is routed to Web Map so the register plate shows its `BERTH_PENDING` words (WM-9: a payload-less `pod_hop` while an unwelded derelict is berthed returns `BERTH_PENDING`, ordered before `TARGET_UNKNOWN`; AC-WM-139); the layer renders no words *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
310	| R7 | any | LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING | any | not read | either | no command and no chart: the refusal words are Web Map's (`IN_TRANSIT`, `BUSY`), shown on the register plate |
311	| R8 | `IN_FLIGHT` | any | any | not read | none exists | no console can be pressed |
312	
313	The POD prompt and the DOCK prompt are **two Interaction CONSOLE subjects, POD_CONSOLE and DOCK_CONSOLE, told apart by Layout's `console_role`** (IA-40; the DOCK subject exists in the home airlock only), because pod at HOME, nothing berthed and a valid pick leave both `pod_hop{pick}` and `berth{pick}` legal, and one `interact` cannot mean both. The split and the table are **agreed 2026-10-28**: Interaction IA-40 (split, DOCK rows `unberth` priority 1 eligible iff `berthed_present()`, `berth` priority 2), Layout LY-23 (`console_role`), Web Map WM-8 / WM-9 (ASK-CT-13, answered) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The prompt wording stays state-neutral (IA-40) and never names a target, distance or cost.
314	5. **Stale-pick echo (drawn by Interaction; ASK-CT-14 ANSWERED 2026-10-28, no longer a gate item)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The echo is drawn by Interaction from this system's host-local read `pick_glyph_key` (the node glyph key the chart draws for the pick; HOME's at a derelict POD press); this system publishes that read and nothing else. Because the pick is invisible at the console and the hop has no confirm, the POD and DOCK plates carry a small text-free echo of the pick (**at R1, from a derelict, the echo is HOME's node glyph**, so the player sees what the irreversible press carries; at R2 and R4a it is the pick's): the pick's node glyph as the chart draws it (the plain rectangle, the Foundry silhouette and, if seen, the tick), nothing else; no name, no ordinal, no distance, no cost (G6 and the CT-44 exception are unchanged). A clear-after-N-seconds timer is rejected (a timeout would change what a press means without the player acting). A playtest observable records presses made with a stale pick (CT-GF-12). Re-opening the chart with focus on the existing pick was considered and **not adopted** (default focus stays HOME; the UX spec may revisit it).
315	The seam (the Adapter injects the host-local pick into the payload at R2 and R4a; a no-pick press at R3 and R4b routes to "open chart") is **accepted** by the Controller (PCI:100 and Interactions row 17) and by Interaction (IA-40) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "provisional" and "degraded if refused" retired; ASK-CT-1 is answered; ASK-CT-13 and ASK-CT-14 were the new asks, both ANSWERED 2026-10-28)*.
316	*Why.* P2 (the commitment at the console, not on a menu); WM-8; an irreversible, fuel-costing write that depends on a hidden host-local pick needs its resolution stated per fact. *Source.* WM-8, WM-21, WM-22, WM:1225, WM:1301; IA-40; PCI Interactions row 17. **-> ADR candidate (d):** the pick-to-console submit seam.

326	| UNSEEN derelict | plain Graphite-lit rectangle (`ui_glyph_node_wreck_plain_24`), no dialect, no tick, no label | yes | yes |

336	**The home-ship composite (the drawing rule for berthed and absorbed records)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) carries, per derelict record, a `home_attach` offset `(dx, dy)` in chart-local art px from HOME's centre to the record's centre, authored so the 24x24 glyph rectangles **share one full edge** (`|dx| = 24, dy = 0` or `dx = 0, |dy| = 24`); "the socket edge" of WM:1083 is that shared edge. The composite is drawn from the existing glyph assets, with no new asset: (a) **berthed**: the record's template glyph at the attach point plus the A17 seam quad on the shared edge; the record is **not** drawn at its authored position while berthed, and returns there on `unberth`; (b) **ABSORBED**: the same glyph at the same attach point in the HOME stroke style, with the seam replaced by the Ground erase quad; (c) the pod marker follows the drawn position of its record. **Berthed and absorbed records are excluded from the snap graph, from focus and from the pairwise `S_MIN` lint of their authored positions**, because they are not focusable; their attach rectangles are linted instead: each must not overlap any other node's bracket-padded rectangle, and HOME plus every attach rectangle must lie inside the chart frame (D.1b). The lint is re-run for each composite state of AC-CT-120: none, B berthed, B absorbed, A and B absorbed. If two records are given the same side of HOME the lint fails the build. Status is read from `web.view` on every change; a record whose status leaves ABSORBED or `berthed` (an `unberth`, or a restore) is simply drawn at its authored position again.

Every glyph is painted in four layers, back to front: the Ground clearing (`NODE_CLEAR_PAD_PX`), the **interior fill**, the **silhouette stroke**, the **outline**; the seam and erase quads come last.

401	*Rule.* One action calls Save/Load's `save_and_quit()`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the call's blocking behaviour is stated.)* **Call contract (this layer's requirement of Save/Load, ASK-CT-7):** the layer disables every item and **presents one frame** before it makes the call, so the disabled styling is on screen before any work; the call must return promptly with `REFUSED_DOWNED` (the same fact as `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`) or `STARTED`, and report completion through a signal or the published `save_status` (`WRITTEN`, `FAILED`) rather than by blocking the frame loop for the write, because a blocked loop freezes the panel and invites an Alt-F4 mid-write. Save/Load's timeout `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is Save/Load's value, default 3 000 ms (range 2 000-15 000) since 2026-10-28; the time to a visible `FAILED` is that timeout, which is within this layer's 3 000 ms ceiling (nothing visible is allowed during the wait, SL-24, and a longer frozen-looking panel invites an Alt-F4 mid-write; ASK-CT-18 answered; Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2, creative-director lean, horror-tone reasons). This layer holds no timer of its own: it never times the write, it reacts only to Save/Load's published facts (`save_status`, `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`); `save_status` is sticky across earlier autosave failures, so `quit_held`, not a stale `FAILED`, is the trigger for a held quit. On `quit_write_active` rising while not already in `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` the layer locks as TX-39. On `quit_held` rising the layer shows `SAVE_FAILED` as TX-23. When the player returns to play (Resume, `chart_table` close, Back to `CLOSED`) while `quit_held` is true or after a `UI3_PLATE` raised by `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, the layer calls Save/Load's `cancel_held_close()` once (idempotent); it does not call it when the exit ends in the Quit-without-saving hold *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*. AC-CT-137 and AC-CT-139 are the checks. **Save/Load's `save_and_quit` itself calls `request_shutdown` after `WRITTEN`, or after an unchanged-state-hash skip that writes nothing (SL-6); the layer calls nothing on that path and never waits on `WRITTEN` as an exit guard.** The item is enabled iff `PauseGate.can_save_quit` (CT-4); otherwise it is disabled (the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7). While the write runs (state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`, this GDD's own label and not a Save/Load name) all items are disabled, `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored, and **nothing is added to the screen**: no spinner, no ring, no bar, no percentage, no toast, no text change (SL UI-2; SL H5; SL-24). Completing the UI-3 hold calls `request_shutdown` once (CR-15) with no write; further input is ignored. `save_status` is a sticky read the layer never clears. `UI3_PLATE` is a full-bleed **message plate** (CT-28) in place of the panel *(orchestrator ruling: UI-3's string is a paragraph and the panel is too narrow for the 45-75 character reading measure at 4 of 6 canvases, ui-programmer finding X1 option (a); OQ-CT-12)*. 403	
404	**CT-22. Hold-to-confirm gesture (closes SL OQ-32 by citation).**
405	*Rule.* Destructive actions (UI-3 quit without saving; UI-5 retire and delete *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) fill a **linear bar with a needle-mark**, never a radial wipe (ART 3.4, 7.3), over the action's hold duration *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `min(CONFIRM_HOLD_S, CT_HOLD_CAP_S)` for UI-3 quit-without-saving and the UI-5 Retire *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*, and `DELETE_HOLD_S` (= 2 x `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`, 1.6 s at authoring) for UI-5 delete; both are Player Controller-owned constants and the second is a **proposed name** (value and range in the Tuning Knobs "cited, not ours" rows; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D81, OQ-CT-30). Every hold-to-confirm also carries the **committed accessibility plan** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80, OQ-CT-8): a two-tap alternative (PCI:835) and an adjustable hold duration, delivered at Alpha by the Controller and Accessibility Settings; the MVP layer ships the hold only, but D.2 reads its threshold from the action's effective duration (never a literal) so neither option needs a rebuild of the gesture. The action fires on the first frame the held time reaches it, not on release. Default focus on a screen with a destructive action is its non-destructive item. Release, `cancel`, `chart_table`, the pointer leaving the item, or window focus loss snaps the bar to empty in the same frame and **nothing else happens**; a new gesture needs a new press edge. The fill is a monotonic fill on the layer's UI clock (CT-43), not a flash (HR-13), and it is function rather than decoration so reduced motion does not remove it. Formula D.2.
406	*Clarification.* PCI:656 says "hold timers (confirm bar, name reveal) are frozen with the pause". That sentence concerns the Adapter's **in-world** channel timers; the UI-3 bar must run while the kernel is `PAUSED`, because the Chart Table is the only thing awake then. Routed to the Player Controller as a wording clarification (C15).
407	*Source.* SL UI-3, UI-5; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-14; registry `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`; PCI:835.
408	
409	**CT-23. Main menu (UI-4).**
410	*Rule.* The boot menu has four items in fixed order: **Continue, New campaign, Display & Comfort, Quit** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Display & Comfort is added so the comfort and photosensitivity toggles are reachable after the first launch without entering a live world, which is the reason the layer exists; it reuses S6, TX-36, TX-37, AC-CT-122)*. Continue is shown disabled (not hidden) when `campaign_info()` returns nothing; default focus is Continue if enabled, else New campaign. Continue shows exactly Save/Load UI-4's SIM facts as words, **without `RISKY`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: playtime (D.7, read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), crew count, kind (`AUTO` / `EVENT` / `QUIT`) and `depth_label` (`RING <n>`).
411	*`RISKY` is not on the Continue line — ruled* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): `RISKY` is dropped from the player-facing Continue line (OQ-CT-31, D82; the creative-director's lean is adopted). It is a fact about the **file** (the generation was written while a soft gate condition was closed, SL-6), not about the world, and it could read as a world-danger or tell-state leak onto the truth layer (a breach was open when the record was written) with no decision attached to it (a single Continue). It stays in `SaveInfo` and in the Debug Overlay; this layer neither reads nor draws it, and the Continue line is exactly playtime, crew count, kind and `RING <n>`. Save/Load's UI-4 is amended to match (hand-off note). **`RING <n>` is the ring of the newest record's pod / home position at the time that record was written; it is never a maximum, a historical "deepest reached" or any running aggregate over the campaign** (G5; a later record at a shallower ring shows the shallower ring; AC-CT-113). No thumbnail, no completion figure, no wall-clock "last played" beyond file metadata. The UI-7 line is shown under Continue on menu entry iff `campaign_info()` reports the newest generation failed verification (`newest_failed_verification`, accepted by Save/Load SL-21; ASK-CT-5 answered). One Continue serves the one logical autosave: the generation chain is invisible and never chosen (UI-4's own wording uses another noun; the stale-token lint allow-list carries it). Vocabulary is Save/Load's only (SL:993). `new_game(world_seed)` takes its seed from Save/Load's boot rule; the menu has no seed field (OQ-CT-6). The backdrop reuses the depth-ring plate and the ring-1 filament sheet with **no nodes** (a node would imply a save state or leak a Continue fact); fallback plain Ground. No title art, logo animation or tagline.
412	*Source.* SL UI-4 (SL:1000), SL-21 (SL:261); ART 2.11.
413	
414	**CT-24. New campaign, UI-5, no beam picker.**
415	*Rule.* New campaign with no existing campaign calls `new_game(world_seed)` directly (via CT-42). With an existing campaign it opens the **UI-5 screen** itself: items **Back** (**default focus**), **Retire** (**under hold-to-confirm at `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: at MVP the player experiences it as irreversible, because Continue stops listing the campaign and there is **no un-retire screen**; the file stays on disk but nothing in the game brings it back, and no text calls it "reversible" or "archived"), and **Delete** as a separate explicit action on the same screen under the longer hold (CT-22). The UI-5 sentence (a `ct.*` key, copy the UX spec's and narrative director's) states plainly what each item does to the player's ability to continue: Back keeps the campaign and Continue still lists it; Retire (hold) takes it off Continue and the game cannot bring it back; Delete (longer hold) destroys the file *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the word "Retire" suggests a recoverable archive, so the vocabulary is routed to Save/Load (OQ-CT-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the default moves from Retire to Back, because the old default let a double-tap on New campaign retire the campaign; the fresh-press-edge rule of CT-41(1) now applies to **every** boot transition, so the press that opened UI-5 never activates an item on it)*. Retire and delete call `retire_campaign(campaign_id)` / `delete_campaign(campaign_id)`; the retired state `RETIRED` is caused by this layer (SL T-9, SL:430). The retired file survives and Continue stops listing it (AC-CT-128). The Delete hold is **longer than the quit hold** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): Delete (UI-5) holds `DELETE_HOLD_S` = 2 x `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 1.6 s at authoring (OQ-CT-30, D81), while quit-without-saving (UI-3) keeps `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` (0.8 s). Delete is the one action that destroys the file with no recovery even by hand, so it asks for twice the hold of the quit that leaves the file on disk; D.2 works the arithmetic. The destructive items (Retire and Delete) look like every other list item (no red, no warning mark) and are distinguished by the bar only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. No campaign list, Records page or un-retire screen at MVP (OQ-CT-4: a retired file stays on disk and is recoverable by file only until an Alpha screen; no text calls retire "reversible"). No beam-shape picker: New campaign calls nothing beyond `new_game`; seat defaults are Suit & Equipment's (SE-9: seat 1 `BEAM_WIDE`); a `NewCampaignOptions` seam is reserved for the VS-B picker (SE:189 calls it optional).
416	*Source.* SL UI-5 (SL:1001); SE-9 (SE:189).
417	
418	**CT-25. Load-failure screens (boot-flow).**
419	*Rule.* UI-8 (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`: a plain statement that no readable record exists, with New campaign and Quit, in that order) and UI-9 (incompatible build: message, New campaign and Quit, in that order, never overwrite or repair; the item order is the same on both screens, which removes the earlier flip between UI-8 and UI-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* are **boot-flow screens**: no pause is requested because the kernel is not `RUNNING` when the failure is reported (SL:1004 says "Chart Table issues the pause"; that wording is stale, C7). UI-7 (corrupt newest record) is one plain ship-log line under the Continue entry **iff** `campaign_info()` reports that the newest generation failed verification (`campaign_info().newest_failed_verification`, SL-21; ASK-CT-5 answered); otherwise the line is HUD & Suit Layer's on the first `RUNNING` frame (SL:1003 lists both owners; this GDD owns the main-menu instance only). New campaign from UI-9 calls `new_game(world_seed)` through CT-42 without opening UI-5; Save/Load creates a different directory and the `READ_ONLY` campaign is never retired, deleted or written (SL:752, SL T-9). Placeholder strings are Save/Load's (SL:1003-1005); final copy is this GDD's `ct.*` table with UX and narrative sign-off. No icon, no red, no dialog chrome beyond the standard Ground plate.
420	*Source.* SL UI-7..UI-9; SL:770.
421	
422	**CT-26. FAULTED in release.**
423	*Rule.* The destination is the boot-flow **main menu** (UI-4) with Continue offered, focus on Continue: in `FAULTED` the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save (KRN:151), so the newest verified generation is intact. Whether a one-line notice accompanies it is OQ-CT-5 (routed to the kernel and Save/Load); this GDD invents no string. Dev builds halt with the Debug Overlay (not ours). PIPE:269 says release "returns to the chart table" and KRN:151 says "returns to the menu"; the wording is reconciled by this rule and routed (C14).
424	*Source.* KRN:151, :940; PIPE:269.
425	
426	**CT-42. The load sequence: black before work.**
427	*Rule.* Accepting Continue, New campaign, Retire (then New) or Delete (then New): (1) all items are disabled and the layer's plate is removed in the same frame; (2) layer 1 black is shown (PIPE row 1: shown in `TRANSIT_HOLD` and `BOOTING/LOADING`); (3) at least one frame at full black is presented (the mechanism is the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` guarantee, `t_hold_pad` of at least 120 ms, which the layer awaits before step (4); the layer does not count frames itself, and the test hook is the frame-capture hook of AC-CT-60; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); (4) only then is `continue_campaign()` / `new_game(world_seed)` called; (5) the first `RUNNING` frame is a camera `CUT` (PIPE:264) and the layer leaves `LOAD_HOLD` for `CLOSED` (TX-33). Nothing is drawn between (2) and (5): no text, no tip, no bar, no spinner (SL UI-6). If the call returns UI-8 or UI-9 the layer re-enables itself on that boot screen (TX-11); if `new_game` (or any other call) fails it re-enables itself on the main menu with one plain ship-log line under New campaign (placeholder copy "Could not start a new campaign.", final copy the UX spec's and the narrative director's; TX-34, OQ-CT-17 closed). A load that fell back from a corrupt newest generation is not a failure: it proceeds to `RUNNING` and the UI-7 line is the HUD's on the first `RUNNING` frame (CT-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
428	*Why.* A restore called with a visible, focused menu would freeze that menu for the whole restore, and a long non-pumping call can mark the window "not responding" on Windows (NOT SOURCEABLE). Save/Load has answered ASK-CT-7: the kernel's restore and every `post_restore()` run as one blocking call inside `LOADING`, never chunked, and the one presented black frame is the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` guarantee (`t_hold_pad`); the rule needs only that one black frame, never progress *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
429	*Source.* SL UI-6; PIPE:99, :264, :278.
430	
431	#### F. Registrations, strings and access
432	
433	**CT-27. Zero registrations; submits nothing.**
434	*Rule.* The chart table is an `INPUT_SURFACE` (KRN:111; PIPE:188; PCI:147) that **submits zero commands at MVP**; the class is kept for VS-B guest pause / save requests (KRN CR-15). It registers **no state block, no hook, no command, no mutator**, and introduces no `allowed_when_paused` type (so KRN CR-16's paused-allowed list is unchanged). It reads only `web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status`, `restore_reason`, `campaign_info()` / `list_saves()` and its own host-local state; never `web.leg_timing()`. It calls only the kernel control plane (`request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_shutdown`) and Save/Load's host-local API (`new_game`, `continue_campaign`, `save_and_quit`, `retire_campaign`, `delete_campaign`). KRN:715 offers "a chart-table command with a path array" as a `MAX_PAYLOAD` example: that example is stale (C3) because this layer submits no command.
435	*Source.* KRN CR-15; SL-21; WM:300; SL-17 (the zero-block precedent).
436	
437	**CT-28. Strings, faces and fit.**
438	*Rule.* All user-visible strings are keys in a closed `ct.*` table owned here (`tr()`), ship-log register, no composed fragments (a value token such as a time is allowed inside one whole string), no exclamation marks, no emoji, Save/Load's vocabulary only. **Instrument face** (bitmap, integer `H`): a closed string set, declared in the `ct.*` table, of `IN TRANSIT`, numerals, keycap letters and short state words; **reading face** (vector, continuous scale): panel item labels, settings copy, the notice, messages and every sentence (ART 7.1). Type and contrast floors are ART 7.1's, by name (menu body, section heading, title, label and caption floors at 1080p / 1440p; text 4.5:1, glyphs 3:1). Each key carries a **fit class**: `LABEL_1` (one line at every canvas row), `LABEL_2` (up to two lines) or `PARAGRAPH` (message plates only, full-bleed Ground sized to the text with the ART 7.1 line-length measure). A lint measures each key with the real faces at each canvas row of CT-16 and fails a `LABEL_1` that overflows; a menu label is never truncated or ellipsised (a clipped "Save & Qu" on the truth layer would read as a lie) and never wraps to a third line.
439	*Source.* SL:127, :993, :1008; ART 7.1.
440	
441	**CT-29. Audio: requests only.**
442	*Rule.* This layer owns and specifies no sound. It requests from Adaptive Audio a UI-bus focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the queued-re-open acknowledgement `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (CT-3) (AA:562: "menu and map sounds are UI-bus, ducked out of the world mix on open; pause suspends all sim-derived sounds"); nothing for open, save or load. `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` is one-shot, on the `ui` bus, with no visual twin, no sanity-stage or Attention dependence, and identical at `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` 334 and `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` 1000; the Chart Table requests it on the press frame that puts a raise into the empty re-open queue, or replaces the queued raise with a different desired raise, once per queued raise; it is SILENT for an idempotent repeat of the same desired raise, for `cancel` of the queue, for the frame on which the queue applies the raise (the plate is the feedback), for a raise that applies at once (no lower within the interval) and for a `request_restore` that clears the queue (TX-27) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. Ducking on open and suspension of sim sounds on pause are Adaptive Audio's. Silent menus are acceptable at MVP. No sanity or Attention effect on menu audio. The master volume control (CT-18, Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D85) only publishes a step through the `SettingsStore`: the bus, the step-to-gain law, the default, the muted state and any cue played at the new level are Adaptive Audio's, and the layer plays nothing itself *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
443	*Source.* AA:562, AA:1086; HR-6. *(provisional — Adaptive Audio owns the cues.)*
444	
445	**CT-30. Accessibility at MVP (structural).**
446	*Rule.* Now: opaque Ground plates (HR-2), focus as a shape (HR-11), ART 7.1 type and contrast floors (HR-12), gamepad completeness of every flow including the chart snap and every destructive action (HR-14), no colour-only state (SL:1010), and an **accessible name on every interactive control** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "a text label on every control" was false for chart nodes, which by CT-14 carry no label)*. **Every focusable chart node is a `Control` with an accessible name equal to its neutral ordinal** (the `ct.compact.slot_<n>` key form of CT-44, **nothing drawn**, so G6 and CT-14 hold in the spatial layout); a node is never built as a bare quad, so adding the AccessKit wiring later forces no rebuild. Every other control's accessible name is its visible `ct.*` label. Mouse and touch players get a signal for what is selectable through the **pointer cursor** change over selectable nodes only (CT-45; OQ-CT-9 closed). At Alpha (Accessibility Settings / Settings): AccessKit wiring (NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference; an ADR (e) spike item), hold-duration and two-tap alternatives for every hold-to-confirm (the destructive holds of UI-3 and UI-5; the Controller's two-tap option, PCI), HUD opacity floor, reading-face scale, HUD scale. **Accessibility tier: standard** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): OQ-CT-8, D80). `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist yet and is to be authored later with `/ux-design accessibility` (it is not created here); until then the layer targets the structural compliance listed above plus the committed Alpha items: a two-tap alternative and an adjustable hold duration for every hold-to-confirm (CT-22), and reduce flashing ON by default (CT-19, a user ruling).
447	*Source.* ART HR-2, HR-11, HR-12, HR-14; SL:1010.
448	
449	#### G. Negative requirements (each its own rule, each with an acceptance criterion in Acceptance Criteria)
450	
451	**CT-31. No Attention surface.** *Rule.* No Attention indicator, meter, tier, hint or glyph on any chart, panel or menu surface, under any setting; depth rings are shown as place, not as attention; no Chart Table surface displays or sonifies the Attention level, tell progress or a Horror's proximity (AA:1515); no per-write autosave mark (its absence would be a hidden Attention meter, SL:965). *Source.* AT:1373, AC-AT-61, AC-AT-66; AA:1515 (Adaptive Audio UI Requirements, "depth rings are place, not attention"); ART 7.4.
452	**CT-32. No horror element (Pillar 3).** *Rule.* No horror, horror position, threat bar, proximity indicator, direction, off-screen arrow, countdown, "last seen" pin or target ring on any chart or menu surface, **under any accessibility setting**. *Source.* HE:377, :1353, :1358, AC-HE-119; Pillar 3 (Attention is shown in the world, never as a meter).
453	**CT-33. No loot value, no remaining-salvage count.** *Rule.* The Chart Table picks the target and shows only what the crew lit, and never reveals; this confirms Boarding's provisional contract (BS:334, Dependencies row 17b); no loot value, no remaining-salvage count (BS:334; BS:1204's wording "and the fuel the hop will cost" is overruled by CT-35, C1). *Source.* BS:334, AC-BS-47c (BS:1427), WM-28, ART 7.4.
454	**CT-34. No sanity indicator.** *Rule.* No sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour on any surface of this layer, including under accessibility settings; save and pause surfaces are never a hallucination class. *Source.* SN:1350, :1357, AC-SN-83, SL H6.

content.content:
455	**CT-35. No fuel, time, ETA, danger or "recommended".** *Rule.* No fuel figure, travel time, ETA, danger rating or "recommended" marker anywhere on the chart; `web.view` structurally lacks the data and the chart never reads `web.leg_timing()`. Boarding's row BS:1204 ("the Chart Table shows what the crew lit and the fuel the hop will cost") conflicts and **Web Map & Transit governs** (WM:1049, WM-35, AB-5; routed to Boarding to reword). *Source.* WM:1049, :1299, :1305; WM-36; C1.
456	**CT-36. No save decoration.** *Rule.* No per-write autosave mark, thumbnail, spinner, percentage, death screen, "progress saved" toast or loading text or tip. Load is layer-1 black via `TRANSIT_HOLD` (UI-6), then a camera `CUT`; this layer adds nothing after a death-stub restore; the **HUD** owns one plain ship-log line on the first `RUNNING` frame, keyed on `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB`, through its `FIRST_FRAME_LINE` channel, with no death wording (placeholder copy "Restored from the newest record.") *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): SL OQ-46 option (b), OQ-CT-33, D84; a death-restart with no text can read as a crash or a rubber-band, which sits badly with the tone row "plain honesty about the cost". The line is the HUD's, so the layer still shows no death screen, counter or word *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Source.* SL H5, SL:965, SL-24 (SL:267); SL UI-6; ART 2.10.
457	**CT-37. No inventory, weight or loadout screen.** *Rule.* No inventory, weight readout or loadout screen. The Sanity evidence list (SN:1350, SN:1357) names "the inventory" and "the death/restore screen"; neither exists (IDB R8; SE:1289; SL; ART), routed to Sanity (C8). *Source.* IDB R8 (IDB:1065, :1320); SE:1289, :1317.
458	
459	#### H. Reserved slots and the rules added by the specialists
460	
461	**CT-38. Reserved slots (no stub art, no layout space at MVP).**
462	
463	| Slot | Owner and phase | Constraint carried |
464	|---|---|---|
465	| Crew beam-shape glyphs on the chart; left-edge text chat | Co-op Session / Chat (VS-B) | ART 7.4, 7.5; risk K1 |
466	| Knowledge Codex annotations | Codex (VS) | each annotation needs a stated effect on play (IDX:47) and is never a lore dump on the truth layer; PROFILE scope |
467	| Post-loss UI read at the chart table | Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A) | ART 7.4 "Loss" |
468	| Onboarding flow after the notice | Onboarding (VS) | `POD_NOT_READY` reserved in Web Map & Transit |
469	| Beam-shape picker | VS-B | `NewCampaignOptions` seam |
470	| Records page, un-retire | Alpha | OQ-CT-4 |
471	| Full PR-14 settings UI, rebinding, HUD scale | Settings & Input Rebinding (Alpha) | MVP hooks with defaults |
472	
473	**CT-39. Narrow truth.** *Rule.* The layer displays only facts that no hallucination class can lie about. Every field it draws is listed with its source (`web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status`, `restore_reason`, `campaign_info()`, the `SettingsStore`) and with the statement that no hallucination class touches it; a fact that any class can falsify (Graph state, entity presence or position, salvage contents or value, a crewmate's rendered form or location) never enters the layer. *Why.* A true copy of a falsifiable fact on a free, pausable menu would make that lie free to disprove, and P4 requires that checking cost time, risk or trust. Review test: *if a hallucination could make the world disagree with this field, the field does not belong here.* *Source.* CON:261-265; Player Fantasy "Under hallucination".
474	
475	**CT-40. Constant drift, constant depth.** *Rule.* The filament drift step and the ring tones are independent of every simulation read and of Attention, depth, sanity and session time; the only inputs to the drift are the layer's UI clock and the reduced-motion toggle. *Why.* P3 names "filament movement" as an in-world Attention sign; a chart filament that modulated would be a meter. *Source.* AT:1373; ART 2.11.
476	
477	**CT-41. Input hygiene around the irreversible press.**
478	*Rule* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: guards (1) to (3) and (5) are enforced by the Adapter's MenuInput feed, CT-45; the layer states the behaviour it needs and consumes the events)*. (1) **Fresh press edge.** When the layer is opened by a console press or by a released governor raise, every activation on it requires a press edge that begins after the open frame; the open press's release, its auto-repeat and any carried-over held state are ignored (the Adapter latches them, CT-45). (2) **The closing activation is consumed.** When `interact` on Resume, `chart_table` or `cancel` at depth 1 closes the layer, the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again; gameplay sees no `interact` edge until a fresh press. The layer **cannot** enforce this alone, because the Adapter polls and resyncs on resume. (3) **Echo ignored.** The Esc / Start toggle's key echo is suppressed by the Adapter, so a held Esc does not flicker the layer. (4) **No click-outside.** A `POINTER` DOWN or UP on the frozen world outside the panel does nothing (the world is a held frame, and a click there would read as an in-world action). (5) **Focus loss.** The Adapter's `FOCUS_OUT` aborts any hold fill and clears navigation state; on `FOCUS_IN` the layer stays open with the previous focus and the kernel state is unchanged.
479	*Why.* The next `interact` edge at the pod console is `pod_hop`, the irreversible act (WM:1225). PCI resends intents on resume and keeps a hold-mode channel only if the button is physically down, so the latch belongs to the Adapter and the layer's requirement is stated here. Key-echo detection and focus-out notifications are NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference (ADR candidate (e)).
480	*Source.* WM:1225; PCI:656-658.
481	
482	**CT-43. The layer's UI clock.**
483	*Rule.* Layer 3 keeps its own presentation-time accumulators driven by the render delta, independent of the kernel state, of `present_time` (frozen under pause, PIPE:265) and of `SceneTree.paused` (ADR candidate (a)): one per hold gesture (starts at press, resets on release, abort or focus loss) and one drift step timer and table index (`acc_us`, `i` of D.5) that persist across opens *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so filaments do not rewind on re-open *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Every delta is clamped to `UI_DT_MAX_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` so a hitch cannot complete a hold or jump the drift. The clock is presentation time (KRN CR-11) and never enters the simulation; no wall clock enters any rule except these presentation timers.
484	*Source.* KRN CR-11; PIPE:265.
485	
486	**CT-44. The compact layout and stable order.**
487	*Status: **DEFERRED-REACHABLE*** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `H_default` every supported window (minimum 1280 x 720, registry `MIN_WINDOW`) gives `m >= 1` (D.1b "Minimum window"), so a player cannot reach the compact list at MVP; it is built and tested through the forced-`H` hook and becomes player-reachable with the Alpha HUD scale or a window delivered below the minimum. This rule, S4, the neutral ordinals, ASK-CT-10 and AC-CT-30 / AC-CT-112 are tagged accordingly.
488	*Rule.* The layout is **compact iff the chart multiplier `m` (D.1b, the fit inequalities) is below 1**, i.e. the frame plus its margins no longer fits the canvas; nominally that is a canvas narrower than 320 HUD px (`COMPACT_LAYOUT_MIN_CANVAS_W`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, **derived** as `CHART_FRAME` width / 0.9, with the height twin 180 = 162 / 0.9; informational since the fit form replaced it as the input to `m`) or shorter than its twin; it is chosen at open and on canvas change, never mid-animation. The list holds at most `N_max_compact` rows (3 at the smallest canvases, D.1b). Then the spatial map is replaced by a **vertical node list** in the ART 7.4 menu grammar: one column of chamfered-rectangle items, Ground interiors, 1-px Graphite-lit borders, the bracket and bezel thickening for focus, each item carrying its 24x24 node glyph at left (the unknown tick drawn inside the silhouette exactly as on the map) and a **neutral positional ordinal** at right (a slot mark, below). The ring plate's Ground, border and rivets remain; rings and filaments are not drawn. The planned-sortie relation is a Tungsten dashed rule under the picked row (no new asset, no fill). The `IN TRANSIT` word keeps its fixed top-left position. **The compact label is a neutral positional ordinal and carries no identity.** It is one whole `ct.*` key per authored layout slot (`ct.compact.slot_<n>`, `n` = the record's position in the layout file, HOME included; no composed fragment such as a word plus a number, CT-28), rendered as the plain ordinal for that slot. It must not be a name, a dialect, a template word or a status word, and it never varies with `status`, `kind`, `template_id`, depth ring or map distance: **an UNSEEN row and a SEEN row render the identical key form**, and a record's key does not change when it becomes SEEN, BOARDED, `berthed` or ORPHAN. The key is bound to the layout slot and is not renumbered when an ABSORBED record leaves the list (a gap in the ordinals is a fact the list already shows, and a stable slot mark lets the player remember which row is which). The ordinal order is lint-checked like positions (no correlation with any Web Map & Transit cost; AC-CT-112). This is the single permitted exception to G6 and CT-14 ("except the CT-44 neutral ordinal in the compact layout, which is not a name"); it is **not** precedent for any further label. WM:1044 (UNSEEN "no dialect, no tick, no label beyond what selection shows") is read as forbidding identity, which a slot mark does not carry (text-label rule of CT-30; **accepted by Web Map & Transit**: its UNSEEN drawing row names the neutral ordinal as the single exception, ASK-CT-10 answered). **Order is a ranking proxy and is therefore fixed:** the list is in stable authored order, HOME first, derelicts in layout-file order; it is never sorted by status, distance, fuel, danger, recency or seen/unseen; an ABSORBED record leaves the list (it is part of HOME now), an ORPHAN stays in its slot, non-selectable; the relative order of the remaining rows never changes. Rows are never truncated; if the list cannot fit, the canvas minimum was mis-set.

493	**CT-45. Menu input feed (Adapter-owned)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new rule)*.
494	*Rule.* **The layer never reads a device.** The Input Adapter (Player Controller & Input PC-1(a)) owns every device read and publishes a presentation-side **MenuInput** event stream on **render frames** (the layer runs on its own UI clock while the kernel is `PAUSED`, CT-43; the Adapter's physics-callback sampling serves gameplay intents only). The stream is the layer's only input, because the Controller's locked lint allows `Input.`, `InputMap.`, `InputEvent` handling, `_input(`, `_unhandled_input(` and `is_action_*` only inside the Adapter's registered files (PCI Acceptance, source-scan criterion). Events: `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT; `source` STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD); `ACCEPT_DOWN` and `ACCEPT_UP`; `BACK`; `CLOSE`; `FOCUS_OUT` and `FOCUS_IN`; `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`; `POINTER{kind MOVE|DOWN|UP|WHEEL, button, position in picture coordinates}`.
495	- **The Adapter also owns**: (1) **echo suppression** (a held key's OS echo produces no second event; CT-41(3)); (2) **deadzone hysteresis** (`MOVE_DEADZONE` to take an edge, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` to release it); (3) **the cardinal-axis rule** (a stick yields one NAV direction at a time: the axis with the larger magnitude, a tie going to the vertical axis, and the taken direction changes only after the stick has re-passed `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, so a diagonal drift cannot alternate between two directions); (4) **latch-until-released** for any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume's accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`): the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it has been physically released and pressed again. This is the consume-the-closing-activation guard of CT-41(2), enforced where the resume resync lives (PCI resends intents on `PAUSED -> RUNNING`); for a console press that opened the layer, the open press's release and repeats are latched the same way (CT-41(1)).
496	- **Navigation set, per device.** Stick (cardinal, edge at `MOVE_DEADZONE`), D-pad (four buttons), arrow keys, and WASD (the `move_*` physical controls). **Accept** = the physical controls of `interact` in this context: E, gamepad A, and Enter and Space as additional keyboard bindings of the context's accept. **Mouse buttons produce `POINTER` events only, never `ACCEPT`** (this GDD's requirement): LMB is not an accept in the `chart_table` context. The Controller's `chart_table` note excludes every mouse button (PC-2a, ASK-CT-15 answered, C23 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*; so a pointer click and a pad accept are two paths that cannot both fire for one physical press (EC-CT-15). **Back** = `cancel` (X / B). **Close** = `chart_table` (Esc / Start). The **D-pad is navigation** in this context: the d-pad zoom edges of PC-16 are emitted from `gameplay` and `inspect_card` only (the PC-2 context table: zoom ignored here), so no zoom edge reaches the layer and none must be discarded by it (EC-CT-18). A pad or Deck player moves the bracket on a vertical list by stick, D-pad or the keyboard equivalents, with no diagonal ambiguity.
497	- **Pointer.** The layer hit-tests `POINTER` events against its own rectangles; a click is an activation only when the UP lands on the item that received the DOWN (EC-CT-16; the full activation rules are in "Activation, reveal and focus targets" below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; hover turns a label Tungsten and hides the bracket (CT-6). A selectable chart node shows the **pointer cursor** (a cursor-shape change only, no art, no label), which closes OQ-CT-9.
498	- **One focus model** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The layer's focus is the only focus, and the mechanism is decided here (option 1 of the re-review): **every layer-3 `Control` is created with `focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE` and `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`**, so the engine's focus owner is never a layer-3 `Control`, the built-in `ui_*` actions have no focus to move, and the engine's own hover and click routing never reaches the layer (all pointer input arrives as `POINTER` events, hit-tested by the layer). The layer draws and tracks its single focus itself as a retained control id (the bracket is drawn from that id). The **accessible-focus path** (CT-30) is separate from engine focus: the layer publishes the retained control id and its `ct.*` accessible name to the accessibility layer through the per-item accessible-name properties, with no engine focus involved; whether AccessKit exposes and announces a `FOCUS_NONE` control's name is **[UNV]** and is spike item (2). Layer-3 Controls take no raw `gui_input`, and the layer neither consumes nor relies on any `ui_*` action. The earlier "engine focus may be mirrored" allowance is **deleted**: a `Control` that holds engine focus is exactly what Godot moves on `ui_down`, so mirroring cannot coexist with AC-CT-118. The rejected alternative (option 2, the Adapter consuming `ui_*` in `_input`) would keep engine focus live and add a second consumer to the Adapter's registered files. Engine specifics (the 4.6 split of mouse/touch and keyboard/gamepad focus, `modules/ui.md`; `FOCUS_NONE` Controls and the accessible-name path) are **[UNV]** until the ADR (e) spike on 4.7.2.
499	- **Activation, reveal and focus targets** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (closes the input-model gaps of the replacement model). (a) **Holds.** A hold (Quit without saving, Retire, Delete) starts on `ACCEPT_DOWN` while the item is focused or on `POINTER{DOWN, LEFT}` on the item, and continues while that activation is physically down and, for a pointer hold, the pointer stays over the item; `ACCEPT_UP`, `POINTER{UP}` anywhere, pointer exit, `BACK`, `CLOSE` and `FOCUS_OUT` abort it (CT-22). A mouse-only or Deck-touch player therefore completes every hold flow by pressing and holding the item; a click released before the threshold does nothing. (b) **Activation edge.** Every non-hold activation fires on `ACCEPT_DOWN` (after the CT-41(1) fresh-press rule) or, for the pointer, on `POINTER{UP}` over the item that took the `DOWN` (EC-CT-16); never on `ACCEPT_UP`, and a pointer `DOWN` alone never activates. (c) **Bracket reveal.** When pointer motion has hidden the bracket (PC-13), the first `NAV_DOWN` or `ACCEPT_DOWN` after that motion only reveals the bracket on the retained focus: it moves nothing and activates nothing, so an unseen control is never fired; the next event acts. (d) **Disabled items are focusable but inert** (accept does nothing; the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7); in `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` nothing is focusable and the bracket is hidden (CT-21). (e) **Focus targets after a transition:** TX-23 (to `SAVE_FAILED`): Resume; TX-25: Retry; TX-32 and TX-39 (to `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`): none; TX-19 (back to `PANEL`): the item that led to the screen just left (Chart, Display & Comfort or Save & Quit); TX-37: the Display & Comfort item. (f) **Cursor shape and coordinates.** The layer may not call `Input.` (the lint), so it publishes a cursor-hint request (`POINTER` over a selectable node or an item, else default) that the Adapter applies (PC-2a, ASK-CT-15 answered). `POINTER` positions arrive in picture coordinates (screen px from the picture rectangle's origin; whether the cursor source reports canvas or window px under the Pipeline's `canvas_items` stretch is **[UNV]** until checked in the engine, AC-CT-135); the layer converts to HUD px (`/ H`) for panel and plate rectangles and to art px (`/ k`) for the chart frame (CT-16), keeping the fractional part for hit-testing. (g) **Read phase.** The Adapter delivers one render frame's MenuInput events in arrival order at the start of that frame, before the layer's per-frame update, so a press and the state it acts on are the same frame's.
500	- **Repeat.** Auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's, from `NAV_DOWN` and `NAV_UP`, on its UI clock (D.9).
501	*Why.* A layer that reads devices fails a locked lint; the guard on the irreversible hop (CT-41(2), EC-CT-20) can only be enforced where the Adapter polls and resyncs; and a single focus model removes the parallel `ui_*` path. The decision is owed **before ADR candidate (e)** is written.

577	**Reachability and closure checks (for the acceptance criteria).** Every state has an exit that does not depend on a hold: `HOLD_CONFIRM` exits by release; `UI3_PLATE` exits by `cancel`, `chart_table`, Retry or Back; `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` exits when Save/Load's `save_and_quit` ends the process (SL-6) or by `FAILED` / the timeout of TX-23 (a Save/Load guarantee); the boot-flow screens each offer Quit. There is no state with no player input and no external exit except `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` and `LOAD_HOLD`, both bounded by Save/Load results; `LOAD_HOLD` now has its exits in the table (TX-33 on the first `RUNNING` frame, TX-11 and TX-34 on a failure result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A restore from any state lands in CLOSED (TX-27), and the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` is a camera `CUT` (PIPE:264). **The transition table is data.** It lives in `assets/data/ui/chart_table_transitions.json` (path provisional; one record per TX id with `from`, `to`, `trigger`, `guard_id`, `effects[]`), is the single source the layer's state machine is built from, and is the file AC-CT-93 walks; the expected-edge fixture `tests/fixtures/chart_table/expected_edges.json` (provisional) lists every `(from, trigger, to)` triple of this section, so a missing or extra row fails the build by diff, not by a walker's silence *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
578	
579	**Order of presentation on boot.** TX-2 (notice) precedes TX-3 (menu); the menu precedes any session; the notice is never shown mid-session. FAULTED in release (TX-3) skips the notice when it has been seen.
