621	## Formulas
622	
623	**Scope and determinism statement.** The Chart Table owns no simulation state (CT-27), so none of the formulas below is hashed (kernel D.12 `state_hash`), snapshotted, replicated or fed back into the simulation, and none uses `rng_derive`. They are **host-local presentation arithmetic** on the layer's own UI clock (CT-43): floating-point is therefore permitted, and wherever a formula is integer-only (D.1, D.1b, D.2's accumulator, D.6, D.7, D.9) that is for **pixel exactness and test repeatability**, not for the kernel's determinism rule. The only simulation-derived inputs are read-only integers or enums from `web.view` and `SaveInfo`. Every formula below is evaluated at presentation time and may be called from a test double with no kernel running (CT-4, AC-CT-2). Dependency formulas are cited by registry or owner name, never redefined: the HUD scale `H` and `H_default = max(k, 3)` (Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline D.4, registry `hud_multiplier`), `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` (Player Controller, registry), `HUD_MIN_SCALE` (Pipeline, registry) and the art-bible numbers of section 7 (ART 7.3, 7.4). Notation: `a div b` is integer (floor) division of non-negative integers; `ceil_div(a, b) = (a + b - 1) div b` is integer ceiling division (registry `safe_margin`); `P_w`, `P_h` are the picture rectangle in screen px (Pipeline D.2/D.3); the HUD canvas is `P_w / H` by `P_h / H` HUD px and may be fractional (the Deck is 426.67 x 266.67 at `H = 3`). The six canvas rows are the rows of CT-16, numbered 1-6 in the order they are listed there.

625	### D.1 Panel fit
626	
627	The panel fit formula is defined as:
628	
629	`W_panel = P_w div (3 * H); safe_x = ceil_div((5 * P_w + 99) div 100, H); safe_y = ceil_div((5 * P_h + 99) div 100, H); content_w = W_panel - PANEL_INNER_PAD_PX - safe_x; V_need = 4 * PANEL_ITEM_H_HUD + 3 * PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD + PANEL_RECORD_LINE_H_HUD + n_wrap * PANEL_LINE_EXTRA_HUD; V_avail = (P_h div H) - 2 * safe_y; the panel fits iff V_need <= V_avail`
630	
631	**Variables:**
632	
633	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
634	|---|---|---|---|---|
635	| `P_w`, `P_h` | int, screen px | 1280-3840 / 720-2160 reachable | Pipeline D.2/D.3 (picture rect) | the visible picture, after `keep` or `expand` |
636	| `H` | int | `H_default .. 2 * H_default` | Pipeline PR-12, D.4 (cited; `H_default = max(k, 3)`, `k` the integer world scale, never the zoom step) | the HUD integer scale; at MVP only `H_default` is player-reachable (CT-18) and the rest is reached by the forced-`H` test hook (CT-16) |
637	| `W_panel` | int, HUD px | 71-213 over the six rows | this GDD (ART 7.4 "right third", integer rule of CT-16) | panel width, hung from a right anchor of 1; `W_panel * H` is an integer screen px by construction |
638	| `safe_x`, `safe_y` | int, HUD px | 11-32 / 6-18 | registry `safe_margin` (source HUD & Suit Layer; the 5 % is the art bible's, ab:754; Pipeline PR-2 cites it), cited, not owned here | the safe margin in whole HUD px, rounded **up** per registry `safe_margin` (never below 5 %); the frame fit of D.1b is re-asserted against the larger margin (AC-CT-26). *(Registry value, not an orchestrator ruling; the earlier floor form is retired.)* |
639	| `PANEL_INNER_PAD_PX` | int, HUD px | 2-8, default 4 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD, checkpoint ruling Q18 | inset between the panel's left edge and its content (chamfer border and rivet clearance); `PANEL_PAD_HUD` is retired |
640	| `content_w` | int, HUD px | 56-177 over the six rows | calculated | the width a panel label may use; lint-checked by D.8 |
641	| `PANEL_ITEM_H_HUD`, `PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD`, `PANEL_RECORD_LINE_H_HUD`, `PANEL_LINE_EXTRA_HUD` | int, HUD px | 12-20 / 2-6 / 8-12 / 6-10; defaults 16 / 3 / 10 / 8 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | item height, gap, status-line slot height (the id keeps its old name; the slot is empty except for `FAILED`, CT-17), and the extra height of one wrapped line *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
642	| `n_wrap` | int | 0-4 | the `ct.*` fit classes (CT-28) | total extra wrapped lines across the four items (`LABEL_2` items; a third line is a lint failure) |
643	| `V_need`, `V_avail` | int, HUD px | 83-115 / 108-324 | calculated | stacked height needed and the vertical space inside the safe margin |
644	
645	**Output Range:** `W_panel` 71 to 213 HUD px, i.e. 426 to 639 screen px; `content_w` 56 to 177 HUD px (336 to 531 screen px); the world strip left of the panel is `P_w - W_panel * H`, never below 854 screen px at 1280 wide. The panel fits at all six rows with `n_wrap = 0`; at the smallest canvas (row 6) it tolerates at most `floor((108 - 83) / 8) = 3` wrapped lines in total.
646	
647	| Row | Picture, `k`, `H` | Canvas (HUD px) | `W_panel` (screen px) | `safe_x` / `safe_y` | `content_w` (screen px) | `V_avail` | Chart multiplier `m` (D.1b) | Chart layout |
648	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
649	| 1 | 1920x1080 keep, 3, 3 (also 2560x1440 at `H` 4 and 3840x2160 at `H` 6: same canvas) | 640 x 360 | 213 (639) | 32 / 18 | 177 (531) | 324 | 2 | spatial |
650	| 2 | 1920x1080 keep, 3, 6 | 320 x 180 | 106 (636) | 16 / 9 | 86 (516) | 162 | 1 | spatial (exact fit) |
651	| 3 | 1280x800 expand (Deck), 2, 3 | 426.67 x 266.67 | 142 (426) | 22 / 14 | 116 (348) | 238 | 1 | spatial |
652	| 4 | 1280x800 expand (Deck), 2, 6 | 213.33 x 133.33 | 71 (426) | 11 / 7 | 56 (336) | 119 | 0 | **compact** |
653	| 5 | 1280x720 keep, 2, 3 | 426.67 x 240 | 142 (426) | 22 / 12 | 116 (348) | 216 | 1 | spatial |
654	| 6 | 1280x720 keep, 2, 6 | **213.33 x 120 (smallest)** | 71 (426) | 11 / 6 | 56 (336) | 108 | 0 | **compact** |
655	
656	**Example (row 3, then row 6).** Row 3: `W_panel = 1280 div 9 = 142`, so the panel is `142 * 3 = 426` screen px and its left edge is at `1280 - 426 = 854`, an integer; a literal one-third anchor would put the edge at 853.33 and make the 1-px bezel and seam one screen pixel thicker on one side under `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` (the engine's rounding rule is NOT SOURCEABLE, so the layout does not depend on it). `safe_x = ceil_div((5 * 1280 + 99) div 100, 3) = ceil_div(64, 3) = 22`; `content_w = 142 - 4 - 22 = 116` HUD px = 348 screen px. Row 6: `W_panel = 1280 div 18 = 71`; `safe_y = ceil_div((5 * 720 + 99) div 100, 6) = ceil_div(36, 6) = 6`; `V_avail = 120 - 12 = 108`; `V_need = 4 * 16 + 3 * 3 + 10 + 0 = 83`, slack 25, so the panel fits; with all four items wrapped once (`n_wrap = 4`) `V_need = 83 + 32 = 115 > 108` and the lint fails the string set. Row 1: `W_panel = 1920 div 9 = 213` (639 screen px, one screen pixel short of a true third, invisible).
657	
658	### D.1b Chart frame, chart multiplier and the compact breakpoint
659	
660	The chart frame formula is defined as:
661	
662	`W_c = P_w div H; H_c = P_h div H; safe_x, safe_y from D.1 (margin rounded up); m = clamp(min(max(0, W_c - 2 * safe_x) div CHART_FRAME_W, max(0, H_c - 2 * safe_y) div CHART_FRAME_H), 0, CHART_M_MAX); compact iff m < 1; x0 = (W_c - CHART_FRAME_W * m) div 2; y0 = (H_c - CHART_FRAME_H * m) div 2; node_hud(i) = (x0 + m * pos_x(i), y0 + m * pos_y(i)); S_MIN = 24 + 2 * BRACKET_PAD_HUD; layout lint: for every pair i != j of focusable records, |pos(i) - pos(j)| >= S_MIN` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `m` is defined directly from the fit inequalities; the earlier `P_w div (MIN_W * H)` form floored the minimum canvas while the margin rounds up, so the frame overflowed by one HUD px at, for example, 1920x1083 and 1921x1080)*
663	
664	**Variables:**
665	
666	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
667	|---|---|---|---|---|
668	| `CHART_FRAME_W`, `CHART_FRAME_H` | int, art px (= HUD px at multiplier 1) | 288 / 162 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, derived: the smallest spatial canvas (320 x 180, row 2) reduced by the 5 % margin on each axis | this GDD (checkpoint ruling Q7) | the fixed frame in which node positions are authored (CT-12) |
669	| `MIN_W`, `MIN_H` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: informational)* | int, HUD px | 320 / 180, **derived** | this GDD (checkpoint ruling Q8) | the **nominal** breakpoint at exactly a 5 % margin, `(10 * CHART_FRAME_W) div 9` and its height twin; `MIN_W` is `COMPACT_LAYOUT_MIN_CANVAS_W`. **No longer an input to `m`** (that is the fit inequalities above); kept for the knob table, the registry note and the reader's orientation, and still moves with the frame |
670	| `CHART_M_MAX` | int | 2, fixed | this GDD | the cap on `m` (`H >= k` bounds it at 2 on every reachable canvas; a forced-`H` or an odd window cannot buy a third multiplier) |
671	| `W_c`, `H_c` | int, HUD px | floor of the canvas | calculated | the integer HUD canvas |
672	| `m` | int | 0-2 reachable (H >= k bounds it at 2) | calculated | the chart multiplier, **the largest integer for which the frame plus both margins fits the integer canvas**, applied to positions only; glyphs stay 24x24 at `H` (CT-12) |
673	| `x0`, `y0` | int, HUD px | `>= safe_x`, `>= safe_y` when `m >= 1` | calculated | frame origin, whole HUD px; rings and filaments extend full-bleed outside the frame |
674	| `pos_x(i)`, `pos_y(i)` | int, art px | `0 .. CHART_FRAME_W - 1`, `0 .. CHART_FRAME_H - 1` | `chart_layout.json` (CT-12), authored per `derelict_id` | node centre in frame-local px; never derived from `world_slot`, legs, ticks or distance |
675	| `BRACKET_PAD_HUD` | int, HUD px | 2-6, default 4 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | clearance between a 24x24 glyph and its focus bracket |
676	| `S_MIN` | int, HUD px | 28-36, default 32, derived | calculated | the minimum centre-to-centre distance so brackets never overlap neighbours |
677	
678	**Output Range:** `m` is 0, 1 or 2 over every reachable canvas (`H >= k` bounds it at 2); the layout is spatial iff `m >= 1`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* With `m` defined from the fit inequalities the frame fit is **true by construction on every integer picture**: `CHART_FRAME_W * m + 2 * safe_x <= W_c` and `CHART_FRAME_H * m + 2 * safe_y <= H_c` hold whenever `m >= 1`, and `m` is the largest such integer (capped at `CHART_M_MAX`), so the frame never leaves the safe area (AC-CT-26, and the property test AC-CT-126). The earlier assertion "per reachable canvas row" failed off the six rows because the old `MIN_W` floored while the margin rounds up. **Minimum window.** The window is refused below 1280 x 720 (`Window.min_size`, registry `MIN_WINDOW`, Pipeline PR-1), and at `H_default` (the only MVP-reachable `H`) every supported window gives `m >= 1`: 1280 x 720 gives a 426 x 240 canvas, `safe_x` 22, `safe_y` 12, so `m = 1`. **The compact layout is therefore unreachable at MVP**; it appears only through the forced-`H` hook, the Alpha HUD scale, or a delivered window below the minimum (Pipeline: `k` clamped to 2, picture cropped), so CT-44, S4, the neutral ordinals and AC-CT-30 / AC-CT-112 carry the tag **DEFERRED-REACHABLE** (built and tested through the hook, not reachable by a player at MVP). **Compact capacity.** `N_max_compact = floor((V_avail + PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD) / (COMPACT_ITEM_H_HUD + PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD))` with `COMPACT_ITEM_H_HUD` 28 (`[PLACEHOLDER]`: the 24-px glyph plus 2 px above and below) is 3 at rows 4 and 6 (`V_avail` 119 and 108), which exactly holds the MVP roster (HOME plus two derelicts) and nothing more; a larger roster fails the layout lint (EC-CT-55) until OQ-CT-14 is answered. **Why the integer form:** `0.9 * 320` is not exactly representable in binary floating point and the 1080p `H = 6` canvas (exactly 320 x 180) sits on the boundary.
679	**Node inset and ring membership lint** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `NODE_INSET_ART = 12 + BRACKET_PAD_HUD` (16 by default). Every focusable record satisfies `NODE_INSET_ART <= pos_x <= CHART_FRAME_W - NODE_INSET_ART` and `NODE_INSET_ART <= pos_y <= CHART_FRAME_H - NODE_INSET_ART`, so the bracket and its pad never leave the frame at any `m >= 1` (the pad is in HUD px, positions scale with `m`, so the margin only grows with `m`); and the padded glyph rectangle plus its Ground clearing lies wholly in the ring-1 band (outside the ring-2 outer radius of `chart_layout.json`), so "all MVP nodes sit in ring 1" is a lint, not a hope.
680	
681	**Example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: recomputed with the fit-inequality `m`; the six rows are unchanged)*. Row 2 (1920x1080, `H = 6`): `W_c = 320`, `H_c = 180`, `safe_x = 16`, `safe_y = 9`; `m = min((320 - 32) div 288, (180 - 18) div 162) = min(1, 1) = 1`, spatial (the boundary case), `x0 = (320 - 288) div 2 = 16 = safe_x`, `y0 = (180 - 162) div 2 = 9 = safe_y`. Row 3 (Deck, `H = 3`): `W_c = 426`, `H_c = 266`, `safe_x = 22`, `safe_y = 14`; `m = min((426 - 44) div 288, (266 - 28) div 162) = min(1, 1) = 1`, `x0 = (426 - 288) div 2 = 69`, `y0 = (266 - 162) div 2 = 52`; an illustrative node at frame position (210, 60) is drawn at HUD px (279, 112). Row 1: `m = 2`, `x0 = 32`, `y0 = 18`, the same node at (452, 138). Row 6 (720p, `H = 6`): `W_c = 213`, `H_c = 120`, `safe_y = 6`; `m = min((213 - 22) div 288, (120 - 12) div 162) = 0`, **compact** (deferred-reachable). **Off-row counterexamples that broke the old form:** 1920 x 1083 `expand`, `k = 3`, `H = 3`: `W_c = 640`, `H_c = 361`, `safe_y = ceil_div((5 * 1083 + 99) div 100, 3) = ceil_div(55, 3) = 19`; the old form gave `m = min(1920 div 960, 1083 div 540) = 2` and `162 * 2 + 2 * 19 = 362 > 361`, an overflow of one HUD px; the new form gives `m = min((640 - 2 * 32) div 288, (361 - 38) div 162) = min(2, 1) = 1`. And `P_w = 1921` at `P_h = 1080`, `H = 3`: `W_c = 640`, `safe_x = ceil_div((5 * 1921 + 99) div 100, 3) = ceil_div(97, 3) = 33`, `288 * 2 + 66 = 642 > 640` under the old `m = 2`; the new form gives `m = 1`. Separation lint with illustrative positions HOME (144, 100), A (210, 60), B (80, 40) (not authored content): HOME-A 77.2, HOME-B 87.7, A-B 131.5, all >= 32. Content-lint corollaries: every record has a position, a `home_attach` offset and a stable ordinal, no position is read from `world_slot`, and no authored distance correlates with any Web Map & Transit cost (CT-12).
682	
683	**D.1c Display & Comfort page fit** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the S6 page had no fit math)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. `ITEM_H_S6 = min(PANEL_ITEM_H_HUD, max(S6_ITEM_H_MIN_HUD, (V_avail - (N_ROWS_S6 - 1) * PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD - BACK_HINT_H_HUD - n_wrap_S6 * PANEL_LINE_EXTRA_HUD) div N_ROWS_S6))`; `V_need_S6 = N_ROWS_S6 * ITEM_H_S6 + (N_ROWS_S6 - 1) * PANEL_ITEM_GAP_HUD + BACK_HINT_H_HUD + n_wrap_S6 * PANEL_LINE_EXTRA_HUD`; the page fits iff `V_need_S6 <= V_avail` of D.1. `N_ROWS_S6` = **6** (the three-choice display-mode list is three rows, plus the two switches, plus the master-volume row of D85), `BACK_HINT_H_HUD` = 10 HUD px (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 8-12, the Back hint line), `S6_ITEM_H_MIN_HUD` = 12 HUD px (the lower bound of `PANEL_ITEM_H_HUD`'s range, fixed), `n_wrap_S6` the wrapped lines of the page's `ct.*` keys. **Derivation of the shrink.** The constraint is that the page fits at every canvas row with `n_wrap_S6 = 0`. Before the master-volume row the page needed `5 * 16 + 4 * 3 + 10 = 102` HUD px and fitted row 6 (`V_avail` 108) with 6 to spare. One more row at the default item height costs `16 + 3 = 19`, so six unshrunk rows need `6 * 16 + 5 * 3 + 10 = 121`: that fits rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 (`V_avail` 324, 162, 238, 216) but not rows 4 and 6 (119 and 108), which are the compact, DEFERRED-REACHABLE rows (D.1b; unreachable by a player at MVP). The item height therefore shrinks on those rows, and only there, to `(V_avail - 5 * 3 - 10) div 6`. **Worked example.** Row 6 (`V_avail` 108): `(108 - 15 - 10) div 6 = 83 div 6 = 13`, so `ITEM_H_S6 = min(16, max(12, 13)) = 13` and `V_need_S6 = 6 * 13 + 15 + 10 = 103 <= 108`, slack 5. Row 4 (`V_avail` 119): `(119 - 25) div 6 = 15`, `V_need_S6 = 90 + 15 + 10 = 115 <= 119`, slack 4. Rows 1, 2, 3, 5: the quotient is above 16, so `ITEM_H_S6 = 16` and `V_need_S6 = 121`. Because the slack at rows 4 and 6 (4 and 5) is below `PANEL_LINE_EXTRA_HUD` (8), **no key on the page may wrap at those rows** (`n_wrap_S6 = 0`; the fit-class lint treats the page's keys as `LABEL_1` there); at rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 the slack (203, 41, 117, 95) tolerates wrapped lines. The page lives in the panel's column in-session and in the main menu's content column at boot, where the width is not the 71-px panel. 723	### D.3 Snap-to-node
724	
725	The snap-to-node formula is defined as:
726	
727	`d = (x_c - x_f, y_f - y_c); phi = atan2(d.y, d.x) in degrees; delta = ((phi - theta + 540) mod 360) - 180 in [-180, 180); S1 = { c in F : -SNAP_SECTOR_DEG/2 <= delta(c) < +SNAP_SECTOR_DEG/2 }; S2 = { c in F : |delta(c)| < 90 }; chosen = argmin over (dist(f, c), |delta(c)|, ordinal(c)) lexicographically, over S1 if S1 is non-empty, else over S2 if S2 is non-empty, else the focus stays`
728	
729	**Variables:**
730	
731	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
732	|---|---|---|---|---|
733	| `f` | node | the focused node | this layer | where focus is now |
734	| `F` | set of nodes | the focusable nodes except `f` | D.4 plus HOME (CT-11 table) | the candidates; ORPHAN, berthed and absorbed records are not in it |
735	| `(x, y)` | int, frame art px, screen y down | frame-local | `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) | authored positions; `d.y` flips so that up is positive |
736	| `theta` | deg | 0 (right), 90 (up), 180 (left), 270 (down) | the pressed direction | cardinal navigation (CT-5); a `NAV_DOWN{dir}` event from the Adapter's four-way read (CT-45) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
737	| `SNAP_SECTOR_DEG` | float, deg | 60-120, default 90 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the width of the primary sector |
738	| `dist` | float, layout px | >= 0 | calculated | used **only for ordering and never displayed** (WM:1049, ASK-AD-7) |
739	| `ordinal(c)` | int | 1..N | `chart_layout.json` | stable authored ordinal, the last tie-break |
740	
741	**Output Range:** a node in `F` or "stay"; no wrap, no shake, no flash. The half-open interval `[-half, +half)` puts a node exactly on a diagonal in **exactly one** sector (45 degrees belongs to up, not right; 315 degrees belongs to right, not down), so the result is deterministic. `delta` is rounded to four decimals before the comparison so a floating-point 44.99999999 does not decide a diagonal. Content-lint invariant: the snap graph over the authored layout is strongly connected (every focusable node reachable from every other in at most `N - 1` presses).
742	
743	**Example** (illustrative data, not authored content; screen coordinates, y down): HOME (144, 100), A (210, 60), B (80, 40), `SNAP_SECTOR_DEG = 90`. Focus HOME, press right (theta 0): A has d = (66, 40), phi = 31.2, delta = 31.2, in `S1`; B has d = (-64, 60), phi = 136.9, delta = 136.9, out; result **A**. Press up (theta 90): A delta = -58.8, B delta = +46.9, both outside [-45, 45), so `S1` is empty; `S2` admits both (|delta| < 90); distances HOME-A 77.2 and HOME-B 87.7; result **A** (this is why the fallback exists: with three authored points, up from HOME would otherwise be a dead control). Press left (theta 180): B delta = -43.1, in `S1`; result **B**. Press down (theta 270): A delta = 121.2, B delta = -133.1, both outside 90, `S2` is empty: **focus stays** (no wrap). From A, press left: HOME delta = 31.2, result HOME. Stick navigation is edge-triggered at the Controller's deadzone with the repeat schedule of D.9.

745	### D.4 Legal-target mirror
746	
747	The legal-target mirror formula is defined as:
748	
749	`legal_targets(view) = {} if view.transit_state != IDLE or view.pod_at == IN_FLIGHT or (view.pod_at == HOME_ID and any(n.berthed and n.status != ABSORBED for n in view.nodes)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; { n.derelict_id : n in view.nodes, n.kind == DERELICT, n.status not in {ABSORBED, ORPHAN}, not n.berthed } if view.pod_at == HOME_ID; { HOME_ID } if view.pod_at is a derelict id`
750	
751	**Variables:**
752	
753	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
754	|---|---|---|---|---|
755	| `view` | `web.view` | read-only | Web Map & Transit WM-36 (provisional name) | the only input; no other read |
756	| `view.nodes[].kind` | enum | HOME, DERELICT | WM-3 | the roster kind |
757	| `view.nodes[].status` | enum | UNSEEN, SEEN, BOARDED, ABSORBED, ORPHAN | WM-3 | the record status |
758	| `view.nodes[].berthed` | bool | | WM-36 | derived by WM |
759	| `view.pod_at` | record id or `IN_FLIGHT` | | WM-36 | where the pod is |
760	| `view.transit_state` | enum | IDLE, LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING | WM-36 | the machine state |
761	| `HOME_ID` | `derelict_id` | | derived: the `derelict_id` of the `nodes[]` entry whose `kind` is HOME | a derived label, never a constant, never registered |
762	
763	**Output Range:** a set of 0 to N - 1 record ids (the HOME singleton from a derelict). It is WM-4 evaluated for **selectability only**; it is not a validation and not a second copy of WM-9's reason order. **The mirror never reflects `FUEL_LOW`, `BUSY`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` or `CAPACITY`** (CT-9): none of them is a `web.view` field *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `BERTH_PENDING` is no longer in this list; the `berthed` field is read, CT-9)*, and greying a node on low fuel would put a fuel meter on the truth layer. A pure function of one `web.view` snapshot: a test double feeds two views that differ only in fuel and expects identical output (AC-CT-24).
764	
765	**Example.** Pod at HOME, `transit_state` IDLE, A UNSEEN, B BOARDED and not berthed: `{A, B}` (UNSEEN is selectable, bare; WM:1299). B `berthed` and not ABSORBED: `{}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; was `{A}`)* (the chart offers no choice that Web Map's E-36 would refuse; the console answers a POD press in Web Map's `BERTH_PENDING` words, CT-10 R6, OQ-CT-3). B ABSORBED and A ORPHAN: `{}`. Pod at A: `{HOME_ID}`. `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT`, or `transit_state == LEG`: `{}`. The roster {A SEEN, B UNSEEN, C ABSORBED, D SEEN and berthed} with the pod at HOME gives `{}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; was `{A, B}`)*; the same roster with D welded in (ABSORBED) gives `{A, B}`.

767	### D.5 Filament drift
768	
769	The filament drift formula is defined as:
770	
771	`r = FILAMENT_DRIFT_FRACTION * V_DRIFT_CEIL; mean_us = round(1000000 * FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX / r); interval_us(i) = max(STEP_MIN_GAP_S * 1000000, (DRIFT_STEP_INTERVAL_PM[i mod 7] * mean_us) div 1000), with STEP_MIN_GAP_S = FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX / V_DRIFT_CEIL; each UI frame while r_eff > 0: acc_us += min(dt_us, UI_DT_MAX_MS * 1000); if acc_us >= interval_us(i) then one step is applied (n_applied += 1; i += 1; acc_us := 0), at most one applied step per frame; under reduced motion r_eff = 0 and acc_us, i and n_applied hold; offset_px = FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX * n_applied mod P_f; the offset is applied to the ring-1 filament sheet only` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2: creative-director lean, authored irregular step table)* (replaces the three step generators, the gap filter and its pending queue: the mechanism was over-engineered for a 0.5 px/s background that only has to never read as a pulse; the ceiling now holds by construction because every applied interval is floored at `STEP_MIN_GAP_S`)
772	
773	**Variables:**
774	
775	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
776	|---|---|---|---|---|
777	| `V_DRIFT_CEIL` | float, art px per second | the art-bible bound | ART 7.3 and 2.11 (cited, not restated with a value, not registered under a new name) | the ceiling "at most 1 art px per second, current ring only" |
778	| `FILAMENT_DRIFT_FRACTION` | float | 0.25-1.0, default 0.5 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the fraction of the ceiling actually used *(orchestrator ruling: the ux-designer's fraction knob over the ui-programmer's raw rate, because a raw number would be a second owner of an art-bible value, rulings R28; default 0.5 over the ux-designer's 1.0 so the layer sits visibly below the ceiling and "very low energy" holds, ART 2.11)* |
779	| `FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX` | int, art px | 1-2, default 1 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the quantum, so the texture never sits on a half pixel |
780	| `acc_us`, `i` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | int microseconds, int | 0 up; persist across opens | this layer (CT-43) | the step timer and the table index; they hold under reduced motion and do not rewind on re-open (they replace the three accumulators `a_k`) |
781	| `DRIFT_STEP_INTERVAL_PM` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2: creative-director lean, authored irregular step table)* | int per mille of the mean interval, 7 values summing to 7000 | defaults {1400, 600, 1150, 800, 1250, 700, 1100} `[PLACEHOLDER]` (the art-director signs the feel); cyclically adjacent entries differ by at least 250; max / min at least 2 | this GDD | the authored irregular step table, cycled in order; replaces `DRIFT_GEN_WEIGHT_PM` and `DRIFT_GEN_PHASE_PM`. The mean interval is preserved (the entries average 1000 per mille), so the mean rate is `r` whenever no entry is floored. At the defaults the stream repeats every 7 steps (14 s), which is accepted: the only player-facing requirement is that it never reads as a pulse, and no two neighbouring intervals are alike |
782	| `STEP_MIN_GAP_S` | float, seconds | derived: `FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX / V_DRIFT_CEIL` (1.0 s at the defaults) | this GDD from the cited ceiling | the floor of every applied interval; at a fraction of 1.0 the result is **at most one applied step per second** (a floored entry makes the mean rate slightly below 1 px/s), so the art-bible ceiling holds even instantaneously, not only on average *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

791	### D.6 Depth-ring ground steps
792	
793	The depth-ring tone formula is defined as:
794	
795	`tone(i, c) = G(c) - ((2 * (G(c) - V(c)) * i + CHART_RING_STEPS) div (2 * CHART_RING_STEPS)) for i in 0 .. CHART_RING_STEPS and each channel c; ring i + 1 is band i for i < CHART_RING_STEPS; the centre disc is i = CHART_RING_STEPS; ordering contract: for every i and c, tone(i, c) - tone(i + 1, c) >= RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL`
796	
797	**Variables:**
798	
799	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
800	|---|---|---|---|---|
801	| `G(c)` | int, 8-bit channel | (28, 33, 40) = Ground `#1C2128` | ART 4.1, 4.6 (cited) | ring 1, where every MVP node sits |
802	| `V(c)` | int, 8-bit channel | (11, 16, 24) = Void Steel `#0B1018` | ART 4.1, 4.6 (cited) | the centre disc, exactly |
803	| `CHART_RING_STEPS` | int | 1-5 by the contract (the span of 16 units allows `floor(16 / 3) = 5`); default 3, MVP content ceiling 3 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the number of ring bands drawn |
804	| `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` | int, 8-bit units | 2-6, default 3 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD (art-director ruling 5.1, checkpoint ruling Q5) | the minimum per-channel step so adjacent steps survive 8-bit quantisation and a poor panel |
805	
806	**Output Range:** each tone lies between Ground and Void Steel and the sequence is strictly darker inward; the disc equals Void Steel exactly. The formula is the **ordering contract made concrete**: it restates no percentage (ART 7.4 and WM:1050 say "about 4 %", which cannot be satisfied together with "reaches Void Steel"; conflict row C16, routed to the art-bible owner). The tones are derived values, never new palette entries and never registered (R16, R28).

808	**Example** (`CHART_RING_STEPS = 3`, Ground (28, 33, 40), Void Steel (11, 16, 24)): ring 1 (i = 0) = (28, 33, 40) `#1C2128`; ring 2 (i = 1) = (22, 27, 35) `#161B23`; ring 3 (i = 2) = (17, 22, 29) `#11161D`; centre disc (i = 3) = (11, 16, 24) `#0B1018`. Per-channel steps are 6/6/5, 5/5/6 and 6/6/5, minimum 5 >= `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` 3, so the contract holds with margin. The art-director's illustrative tones (24, 29, 36), (20, 25, 32), (15, 20, 28) in the art-director's proposal are one evenly-divided reading over four intervals; the checkpoint ruling (Q5) fixed ring 1 = Ground exactly, so this interpolation governs and the exact on-screen values are verified in the spike (banding check by pixel sampling, AC-CT-47).

Ten presses in one second therefore produce at most three raises and the kernel is paused only while a plate is up. The cost is stated plainly: up to 334 ms of running world with no plate after a rapid re-open. In OVERLAY the sim runs under the plate, so there is no free scan, and the same governor still limits the plate's luminance reversals (CT-3, CT-4).

If a raise is queued and the player releases the key before the interval ends** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the intent is latched and still applies at the interval end (CT-3); the release changes nothing. 1348	**CT-VA-16. Depth steps are an ordering contract, not a percentage (clarification C16).** ART 7.4 and WM:1050 say each step is "about 4 % darker toward centre; the inner ring's centre reaches Void Steel". The arithmetic does not close: Ground `#1C2128` is (28, 33, 40) and Void Steel `#0B1018` is (11, 16, 24), a span of 17 / 17 / 16 units; 4 % relative is about 1.5 units a step (near-invisible after 8-bit quantisation, ART 8.11 flag 1, and it never reaches Void Steel), and 4 points of white overshoots below Void Steel. The governing reading is the **ordering contract of D.6**: ring 1 is Ground itself (the lightest, where every MVP node sits and every contrast check is measured), each ring band is darker than the one outside it by at least `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` per channel, and the centre disc is exactly Void Steel. **The D.6 interpolation governs: (28, 33, 40), (22, 27, 35), (17, 22, 29), (11, 16, 24).** The art-director's first illustrative tones (24, 29, 36), (20, 25, 32), (15, 20, 28) assumed ring 1 below Ground; checkpoint ruling Q5 fixed ring 1 = Ground exactly, so they are superseded and not live values. Exact on-screen values are verified by pixel sampling in the spike (AC-CT-47, banding check at 1080p and the Deck canvas). The "about 4 %" wording is not restated as a value in this GDD; the clarification is routed to the art-bible owner (C16). The tones are derived values, never new palette entries and never registered.

1350	**CT-VA-17. The `IN TRANSIT` word.** Inline on the full-bleed Ground, **no plate** (ART 7.4's register is already Ground). Instrument face (bitmap, 7 art px cap height), Paper White, tabular letterspacing of one art px (ART 7.1). **Fixed frame position**: inside the chamfered border at the top-left, anchored to the picture rect with the 5 % safe margin (PIPE:88); it is a status word like a label on a bezel and is never placed near the origin node, the target node or along the route, because position would read as direction or progress that `web.view` structurally lacks (WM-36). Shown iff `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT` (CT-15); it appears and disappears in a cut with the data; no ellipsis animation ("IN TRANSIT..."), no blinking, no dots. BERTHING shows **no word and no element** (WM:1307). The word is the only text on the chart during flight: there is no "arriving in" and no counter.
1351	
1352	**CT-VA-18. Compact layout (look).** Triggered iff `m < 1` (CT-44, D.1b); the worst reachable canvas is 213.33 x 120 HUD px. Menu-component grammar (ART 7.4): one column of chamfered-rectangle list items with Ground interiors and 1-px Graphite-lit borders; the bracket and bezel thickening as in CT-VA-7; each item carries its 24x24 node glyph at left (`ui_glyph_node_home_24`, `ui_glyph_node_wreck_plain_24`, `ui_glyph_node_wreck_foundry_24`) with the unknown tick drawn inside the silhouette exactly as on the map, and its neutral positional ordinal at right (one whole `ct.compact.slot_<n>` key, CT-44; no name) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **No rings and no filaments** in compact mode (ring steps would be unreadable at 120 art px of height and add draw cost); the Ground plate, border and rivets remain so the layer still reads as the same register. The planned-sortie relation is a Tungsten dashed rule beneath the picked row (1 art px, no new asset, no fill, no new colour). The `IN TRANSIT` word keeps its fixed top-left position. **List order is a ranking proxy** (a vertical list invites "top is best"), so it is the stable authored order of CT-44: HOME first, derelicts in layout-file order, never sorted; this is acceptance criterion AC-CT-31. Rows are never truncated; if a list cannot fit, the canvas minimum was mis-set.
1353	
1354	**CT-VA-19. Filaments and rings: authored (D12), three bands (D20).** (1) Authored, not procedural: ART 3.4 requires branching, non-repeating, no right angles, density rising inward, which is hand-drawn art direction; procedural generation is a VS-A candidate to be revisited only if ring 2-3 content arrives. For MVP: one hand-authored filament sheet for ring 1 (drifting, scrolling by whole-art-px offset with a seamless wrap that creates no visible seam or repeat at any reachable canvas; the sheet is longer than the largest canvas in the drift axis plus one wrap period) and static sheets for the horizon bands. (2) Three bands plus the Void Steel centre disc give the "inward-pulling" composition (ART 2.11) and the Depth Rings of the Vertical Slice then need no layout change. Rings 2 and 3 are horizon only, with static filaments denser toward the centre (ART 3.4), no nodes, no labels, no ticks. (3) Ring 1 is the sparsest band, so the drifting filaments are the sparsest: correct for "very low energy" (ART 2.11).
1355	
1356	**CT-VA-20. Route and dash grammar.** The planned sortie is Tungsten, dashed, 1 art px, dash 2 on / 2 off art px (`ROUTE_DASH`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`), rectilinear segments only (human geometry over inhuman, ART 3.4). ART 7.4 also lists "routes dashed Hull Grey", but the MVP star topology has no standing routes, so the planned sortie is the only route drawn; if non-planned routes ever land (Hull Grey) they must use a different dash pattern, because the Tungsten versus Hull Grey distinction alone is weak in greyscale (shape backup, ART 4.0 principle 2). C12 is closed by Web Map & Transit (`leg_target_id`, `leg_origin_id`, `leg_dir`): the in-flight route is drawn on both legs from `leg_target_id`, `leg_origin_id` and `leg_dir` (OUT: HOME to target; BACK: origin to HOME), with the word `IN TRANSIT` alone only when the needed id is NONE (CT-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G2)*. Routes, seams and rivet lines are **textured quads of a 1-art-px tile**, not width-1 line draws (the 4.7 `CanvasItem` line draw has no antialiasing feather) -> ADR candidate (b), the layer-3 component library.
1357	
1358	**CT-VA-21. Main-menu backdrop.** The main menu and the boot-flow screens reuse the depth-step plate and the ring-1 filament sheet as their Ground backdrop with **no nodes** (a node would imply a save state or leak a Continue fact), the menu column sitting left of the centre disc so the composition still pulls the eye inward behind the list. Fallback if the playtest finds it noisy: plain Ground. No title art, no logo animation, no tagline (anti-pillar: no authored story). A game title, if shown, is a reading-face title (title floor of ART 7.1), Paper White.
1359	
1360	### Type and layout
1361	
1362	**CT-VA-22. Faces and localisation.** **Instrument face** (bitmap, 7 px and 5 px cap, integer `H`): labels, `IN TRANSIT`, the main-menu Continue numerals, `FAILED`, keycap letters (no node labels at MVP). **Reading face** (vector humanist sans; regular plus one heavier weight, no light weights): settings copy, notices, messages, list item labels in menus, titles. Floors are cited from ART 7.1, not restated (Tuning Knobs, cited rows). Both faces carry tabular numerals, a slashed or dotted zero and a distinct 1 / l / I. The bitmap set is a **closed list** (`IN TRANSIT`, digits, `FAILED`, short labels; CT-28; `RISKY` removed 2026-10-27, user rulings, D82): every sentence and any string likely to localise goes in the reading face, otherwise each locale needs hand-drawn bitmap glyphs (R-AD-10). The reading-face scale is continuous (the only non-integer text), so plates are sized to text with a minimum, not text fitted to a fixed plate; a reading-face line is 45-75 characters (ART 7.1); all text sits on an opaque Ground plate (HR-2). Chamfers only, no rounded corners (ART 3.4); one rivet per corner of the border, never as texture; dial arcs absent. Layout is anchored to the picture rect with the 5 % safe margin at every reachable canvas (CT-16). The right-third panel is `W_panel` HUD px wide (D.1); at row 6 it is 71 art px, so labels must fit by reading-face scale or compact behaviour applies: no label is truncated and none carries an ellipsis (CT-28).

Silent menus are acceptable at MVP. The visual mood the audio should match: **hush**. The chart table is the quietest room in the game, a place where nothing is wrong and nothing is being measured; menu and map audio should sit outside the fiction's danger. 1434	### Feel statement
1435	
1436	**CT-GF-1. The feel in one line.** Instant to answer, slow to move, never excited. Every input is answered in the frame it arrives or in the one after; nothing on the layer overshoots, bounces, pulses, shakes, glints or counts down (the three reading motions of ART 7.3 are absent, CT-2); the only autonomous motion is a web drifting at a fraction of one art pixel a second. The pause is a held breath, not a refuge (Player Fantasy, Moment 2): the panel appears without softening the world and disappears without ceremony.
1437	
1438	**CT-GF-2. Feel pillars for this layer.** (1) *Answered*: no input is ever swallowed without a visible or documented reason (a disabled item is shown disabled; `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` ignores input by rule, CT-21). (2) *Held*: the world beneath is the same frame (PIPE:265), so the panel's arrival changes nothing it does not cover. (3) *Deliberate*: the irreversible acts (UI-3 quit, UI-5 retire and delete) cost a full hold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* on a linear bar, and the sortie commitment is off this layer entirely (the console press, CT-10). (4) *Plain*: no easing except the 100 ms bracket, no sound beyond a focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the queued-re-open acknowledgement (CT-3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*.

1465	**CT-GF-4. Mash tolerance** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces "every press is honoured, no cooldown")*. Every **close** is honoured on its press frame and there is no cooldown on any panel item (Resume, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit, Back). A **re-open** pressed within `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` (334 ms; 1000 ms under reduce flashing) of the last close is latched and applied when the interval elapses, plate and kernel pause together, and only `cancel` cancels it; a repeat `chart_table` press is idempotent *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (CT-3 re-open governor, EC-CT-68, EC-CT-77 to 79). The feel is therefore: closing is instant, opening after a recent close can lag by up to a third of a second (a press that is queued and then cancelled with `cancel` has no on-screen effect at all, which a tester must not file as a swallowed input; the queued press itself gives an audio-only acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, never both a plate and a running sim wrongly, and ten presses in one second never produce more than three raises (at most six opposing transitions, `F <= 3` under registry `flash_count`; AC-CT-114, AC-CT-115). (2) Panel edge: `W_panel` HUD px, `W_panel * H` screen px, an integer by construction, so the panel's left edge `P_w - W_panel * H` is an integer screen pixel (D.1: 1281, 1284, 854, 854, 854, 854 for the six canvas rows). Snap-to-node feel (gamepad and keyboard).** A direction press moves focus to the nearest focusable node whose bearing falls in the pressed direction's sector (`SNAP_SECTOR_DEG` 90 degrees), widening to the half-plane if the sector is empty, else staying (D.3). Feel targets: with three nodes, **no direction press is a dead control when another node exists on that side or in the half-plane** (the fallback exists for this); a press with no candidate leaves focus where it is with **no shake, no flash, no sound** (staying is silence, not an error); the bracket never wraps from the last node to the first; the same press always lands on the same node (deterministic, the diagonal assignment is exact, D.3); and every node is reachable from every other in at most N - 1 presses. Mouse and pad are equivalent in outcome: a click on a node is focus plus accept (CT-6). A stick resting on the deadzone boundary produces one move per edge, not a chatter (D.9, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`).

1492	
1493	**CT-GF-9. No juice, by rule.** No squash, scale pop, overshoot, bounce, wobble, shake, flash, glow, pulse, particle, screen-space effect, parallax, slide or wipe on any element of this layer (ART 7.3, rulings R16, CT-2). The press acknowledgement is a one-frame Paper White hold on the label (CT-VA-7). A destructive action looks like every other item until its bar fills. A completed hold fires on the same frame the bar is full; there is no celebratory beat. This is not austerity for its own sake: ornament on the truth layer reads as the layer reacting, and a reacting layer reads as an instrument that can be fooled.
1494	
1495	**CT-GF-10. Stillness as weight.** The panel is a heavy opaque plate, chamfered and riveted (ART 7.4), that does not move once placed; the world beside it is a held frame, undimmed. The contrast (a still true plate beside a world frozen mid-lie at stage 3) is the feel the Player Fantasy aims at (Moment 2). The only life on the chart is the filament drift, kept deliberately below the art-bible ceiling so the screen reads "very low energy" (ART 2.11) and never "something is happening".
1496	
1497	**CT-GF-11. Silence and absence of reward.** No sound on open, save or load; the only cues requested are a UI-bus focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the audio-only queued-re-open acknowledgement `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (CT-3, CT-29), owned by Adaptive Audio *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. No "progress saved", no autosave mark, no completion flourish, no achievement toast, no tip on the black between menu and world (CT-36). Save & Quit's feel is *closing the log*: the items dim, the process ends.

1739	### Gate convention, tags and story types
1740	
1741	**Tags.** `(auto)` = automated unit or integration test with a test double, deterministic, no wall clock. `(lint)` = a static or content lint run in CI. `(review)` = a named reviewer reads a retained artefact against a checklist. `(manual)` = a person plays or inspects, with retained evidence. `(spike)` = measured once on the real display path and real faces, result retained. `(integration)` = run against the real neighbour modules. `(playtest)` = outside testers. `(auto-render)` or `(render)` = an automated render-capture criterion run by the **auto-render job** on a rendering-capable runner (not `--headless`, which cannot read back viewports), compared by pixel mask or numeric log and retained *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Each tag carries its **story type** after a comma (Logic, Integration, UI, Visual, Config), which is how `/story-readiness` resolves the gate level from the coding-standards table.
1742	
1743	**Gate levels (applied once, here).** `(auto)` Logic criteria and `(integration)` criteria are **BLOCKING**. `(lint)` and `(auto-render)` criteria are BLOCKING; **a lint or render AC marked "CI job to be built" is not verifiable until that job exists, the job is its own story and a declared dependency of every story that cites the criterion, and a missing job makes the story BLOCKED, never passed** (the source scans, fit-class measurement, layout-JSON lint, string scans, asset-name scan, scene-id whitelist, palette lint and the auto-render job are all new; gap F-E; the test doubles, hooks and gdUnit4 setup are gap F-H) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the "BLOCKING once the job exists" escape hatch is removed)*. `(manual)` UI and Visual criteria marked BLOCKING need a **retained screenshot** in `production/qa/evidence/chart-table/`: a screenshot captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. `(review)` criteria are BLOCKING when they gate a UI or Visual story, and say so. `(spike)` and `(playtest)` are **ADVISORY** unless stated.

content.content:
*Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel). **Movement closes the card** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D94, the Controller's context-matrix amendment adopted; the In-World Instruments fallback "buffer and replay the first move press" is void)*: a **fresh** movement input in `inspect_card` (a `move_*` key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`) returns the context to `gameplay` **and** submits `set_move_intent` for that octant in the same frame, in that order, so the first press both closes the card and moves the avatar (nothing is swallowed, nothing is buffered). A direction already held when the card opened is latched and does not count until it is released (or the stick falls below the exit band) and pressed again, so opening the card while walking does not close it on the next frame. A move that closes the card while a channel is running is an ordinary non-`NONE` move intent and aborts the channel exactly as it does in `gameplay`. Any transition of `loco_state` to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` returns the context to `gameplay` on the same frame (the Adapter observes the published state; the card or overlay closes and the cursor is hidden again). Pause is reachable in every state including `DOWNED`: `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`. The full **context × action matrix** is in the table below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; supersedes the earlier "cancel all channels on every non-`gameplay` entry" note for `inspect_card` only. Routed to Instruments and Interaction as a cross-GDD note.)* The OS cursor is **hidden and confined** in `gameplay` (HUD HS-52: no cursor in `gameplay`; the beam is the pointer) and **shown and released** in `chart_table` and `chat` (in `chart_table` its shape follows the layer's `cursor_hint`, PC-2a (g)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)*; in `inspect_card` it stays **hidden and inert** (HUD HS-52: `set_aim` stays live there, and a visible cursor would be a second pointer over the beam; PC-16). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer, in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; cursor visibility in `inspect_card` corrected 2026-10-27 — design review, HS-52 owns it)* Zoom is reachable from `gameplay` and `inspect_card`, and pause from `gameplay` (from `inspect_card` the first `chart_table` press closes the card, see the context return table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `chat` (VS-B) swallows text keys and is the only keyboard-only flow in the core loop (HR-14).
*Default bindings (`chart_table` context).* No new action. The Adapter (never the Chart Table) reads the physical controls of `move_up/down/left/right` (WASD, left stick) plus the arrow keys and the d-pad, four-way under `MOVE_DEADZONE` / `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`; accept is the physical controls of `interact` in this context minus every mouse button (E, gamepad A), plus Enter and Space as fixed additional keyboard accept bindings of this context; back is `cancel` (X / B); close is `chart_table` (Esc / Start); every mouse button and the wheel are `POINTER` events only, never an accept. Conflicts are checked per context (PC-13). The gameplay-context `interact` alias LMB (default bindings table) is unchanged. All of it reaches the layer as the MenuInput stream (PC-2a). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)* **Console seam:** at the pod console the Adapter injects the host-local `ChartPick` into `pod_hop`'s payload; a console press with no pick submits nothing and opens the chart (`chart_table` context) instead — a context switch, not a verb choice (Chart Table ASK-CT-1, ASK-CT-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus)*
**PC-2a. MenuInput stream (Adapter-owned; consumer: the Chart Table layer, CT-45).** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)* The Adapter publishes a presentation-local MenuInput event stream while the active context is `chart_table`; before a campaign is loaded (the boot-flow screens) the Adapter runs in the `chart_table` context with no gameplay sink and publishes the same stream. It is sampled on render frames (the physics-callback sampling of PC-1 (a) serves gameplay intents only); all events of one render frame are delivered in arrival order at the start of that frame, before the layer's update. **Events:** `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` ∈ {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}; `source` ∈ {STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD}); `ACCEPT_DOWN`, `ACCEPT_UP`; `BACK`; `CLOSE`; `FOCUS_OUT`, `FOCUS_IN`; `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`; `POINTER{kind ∈ {MOVE, DOWN, UP, WHEEL}, button, position}`, where `position` is the cursor relative to the picture rectangle's origin, which is `cursor_vp` itself (the D.7 variable table measures `cursor_vp` from the world picture's origin, so nothing is subtracted twice), in the unit of `cursor_vp` (D.7 variable table; the unit under the `canvas_items` stretch is **[UNV]** until the spike of Chart Table AC-CT-135 (f) reads it). **The Adapter owns:** (a) **echo suppression**: an OS key echo of a held E, Enter, Space, Esc or X produces no second event (the engine's echo flag is **[UNV]** until the ADR spike); (b) **deadzone hysteresis**: a stick takes a NAV edge on crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` and releases below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, the same band as the `inspect_card` movement rule (PC-2 contexts); (c) **the cardinal-axis rule**: a stick yields one NAV direction at a time, the axis with the larger magnitude, a tie going to the vertical axis; the taken direction changes only after the stick has re-passed the exit band, so a diagonal drift cannot alternate; auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's (Chart Table D.9); (d) **latch-until-released**: for any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`) the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again, including across the `PAUSED → RUNNING` resync (Edge Cases, kernel `PAUSED`); for a console press that opened the layer, the open press's release and repeats are latched the same way; (e) **focus**: `FOCUS_OUT` releases every held menu control and clears navigation state, and the layer's hold fills abort; on `FOCUS_IN` nothing is held and fresh presses are required; (f) **`DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`** is published when the last-used-device glyph set changes under PC-13 (immediately, except inside `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` of the previous change, when it is published at the window end), so the layer adds no delay; (g) **the cursor hint**: the layer publishes `cursor_hint` ∈ {DEFAULT, SELECTABLE}; the Adapter, its only `Input` caller, applies the pointer-cursor shape. The `zoom_*` edges are never emitted in this context (PC-16). The stream carries no gameplay command and no simulation read. Its code lives in the Adapter's registered files (AC-PCI-176).
====
- **AC-PCI-226** **GIVEN** context `chart_table` and a recorded device script, **WHEN** E, gamepad A, Enter, Space, LMB, RMB and the wheel are pressed, **THEN** `ACCEPT_DOWN` / `ACCEPT_UP` are emitted for E, A, Enter and Space only; LMB and RMB emit `POINTER{DOWN|UP, button}` and never an `ACCEPT`; the wheel emits `POINTER{WHEEL}`; Esc / Start emit `CLOSE` and X / B emit `BACK`; no zoom edge and no gameplay command is submitted. - **AC-PCI-227** **GIVEN** a left stick at (0.30, 0.28) with `MOVE_DEADZONE` 0.25 and `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` 0.05, **WHEN** sampled, **THEN** one `NAV_DOWN{RIGHT}` is emitted (the larger axis); a tie (0.30, 0.30) yields the vertical axis; a drift that alternates which axis is larger without re-passing the exit band emits no second direction; releasing below 0.20 emits `NAV_UP` once. | `transit_state` | IDLE, LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING |

On an OUT leg the route is `leg_origin_id` (HOME) to `leg_target_id`; on a BACK leg it is `leg_origin_id` (the departure derelict) to HOME *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `leg_origin_id` added; it is persisted since the re-review, so a restore in a BACK leg can rebuild the astern hull)* |

60	
61	**The crew member the player is here** is the navigator of WM's committed crossing (WM:59, "the navigator's authority and the passenger's exposure in one beat"). Web Map & Transit owns the exposure half (the leg). This GDD owns the authority half, and the authority is honest only because the table is mute about the price.
62	
63	**Framing alternatives considered** (Category UI: direct framing).
64	
65	| | Framing | What it centres | Verdict |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| **A** | **Direct: "The honest table."** A sober human instrument where the player picks, stops and leaves. Nothing on it lies; nothing on it helps more than the crew has earned | P1 truth by layer (ART 7.0 row 3), P5 inward composition, the navigator's authority (ART 2.11) | **Adopted** |
68	| B | "The navigator's bridge": plotting the web as a mastery fantasy; route planning as skill expression | route planning, comparative choice between targets | **Rejected as primary.** The MVP web is a star of at most one hop (WM-4); a plotting fantasy over three nodes either overpromises or pulls cost, distance and ETA data onto the chart to give the plotting something to chew on, which is guard rail G6 below. It also repeats the framing Web Map & Transit rejected for the same reason (WM:78). The *word* navigator is kept (ART 2.11); the *fantasy of plotting* is not |
69	| C | "The refuge": the menu layer as sanctuary, a warm decompression space between horrors | relief, emotional recovery | **Rejected.** ART 2.11 puts the table "inside its mood"; a refuge would dim or soften the world (ART 7.4 forbids it), invite a calming cue (a relief sting is a mood effect, and menu audio carries no sanity or Attention effect, AA:562) and in solo turn the pause into a sanity-recovery exploit by feel even though Sanity reads nothing from it. It contradicts P2: the tell is still there when you come back. It is also Submission, which the concept ranks as "deliberately absent" (CON:89) |
70	| D | Diegetic prop: a physical chart table the player walks to in the home-ship | a place to stand, embodiment | **Ruled out (CT-1).** A prop is a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and is unreachable on a sortie. Recorded so a later stage does not re-propose it as a fantasy upgrade; no in-world schematic console exists: the Controller's Adapter owns the `inspect_card` context and In-World Instruments owns the card's content and draws no schematic (IW-28, C4) |
71	
72	*Why A carries the concept's MDA ranking (CON:82-89):* Discovery (1) is delivered by the chart **growing only by looking** (the Tungsten tick appears only once the unknown was seen from the pod, ART 7.4; WM:85); Challenge (2) by the chart **withholding the price**, so the player must read the Graph's witnesses; Fantasy (4) by the navigator role and the home silhouette growing with each absorbed section (Moment 4). **"And also" test at system scale:** *it is a galaxy map, and also it only remembers what your crew has lit, and it will never tell you what the trip costs.* The second clause sparks the right question ("then how do I know?") and the answer is the world.
73	
74	### Pillars served (verbatim, then scope notes)
75	
76	> **Pillar 1: The World Never Lies.** "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong. [...] *Design test*: a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe → the pipe." (CON:208-221)
77	
78	Primary. The Chart Table serves P1 from the side most systems never touch: it is the one surface in the game that is **not part of the world and therefore cannot be an instrument** (ART 7.0 row 3: "Chart table (meta): nobody in the fiction ... can a reading lie? never"). P1 says only instruments and perception can be wrong; this layer is neither. Its job is to be true *and to say almost nothing*, so that the truth the player needs still has to be read off the pipe.
79	
80	> **Pillar 5: Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total.** "Risk and reward map to depth in the web. [...] *Design test*: safe farming vs. scarcity that pushes inward → scarcity." (CON:272-279)
81	
82	Served by composition, not data: the chart darkens toward the centre ("the horizon the game never lets you reach", ART 2.11 carried element) and carries no completion, percentage or win datum (WM guard rail 5, WM:144). **Scope note (carried from WM:53):** the Chart Table does **not** carry the failure contract's "never knowledge" half. The chart is drawn from `web.view`, which is WORLD-scope and rolls back on restore (WM-28); the pick resets on every restore (CT-8). Nothing in this GDD may be cited as evidence that knowledge survives a failure; the Knowledge Codex (VS) owns that, and its chart annotations are a reserved slot (CT-38).
83	
84	> **Pillar 3: The Web Watches.** "Attention is shown in the world (creaking, flicker, filament movement), never as a hidden meter." (CON:231-237)
85	
86	Served by absence. The pillar names "filament movement" as an in-world Attention sign, and the chart also draws moving filaments. That collision is the most likely way this layer becomes an Attention meter by accident, so it is a named guard (G5, CT-40): **the chart's filament drift is constant and is never modulated by Attention, depth, sanity, time in session or anything else.** "Depth rings are shown as place, not as attention" (AT:1373).
87	
88	> **Pillar 4: Sanity Rewrites Reality.** "**No lie is unfalsifiable**: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust. At least one channel of truth always remains." (CON:261-265)
89	
90	Served twice, and the two halves pull against each other (resolved in "Under hallucination" below): the layer **is** a channel of truth that always remains, and it must **not** become a free way to check a lie, because P4 requires that checking cost something.
91	
92	> **Pillar 2: Dread Before Chaos.** "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived (sound, light, gauge drift, hull stress)." (CON:223-229)
93	
94	Served by keeping the commitment off the menu: the console press is the point of no return (WM:1225; CT-10), the pause is non-diegetic only (KRN CR-16), and the panel never dims, blurs or desaturates the world it freezes (ART 7.4; PIPE:265), so a tell that was on screen when the player pressed Esc is still on screen while they stand at the panel.
95	
96	### Emotional arc across a session at the table
97	
98	Session shape from CON:181-185. Final copy for every surface is the UX spec's and the narrative director's; the register is fixed under "Tone and language".
99	
100	| When | Surface | Target feeling | Must never feel like |
101	|---|---|---|---|
102	| Boot | Photosensitivity notice (CT-20), then main menu (CT-23) | *Plain care.* A notice that asks once and never nags | A legal wall, a splash screen, a countdown |
103	| Session start | Continue line: playtime, crew count, kind, `RING <n>` (SL UI-4, amended to drop `RISKY`, D82) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | *A ship's log, not a trophy case.* "This is where we were." | A save-slot gallery, a thumbnail, a "last played 3 days ago" nudge, a completion bar |
104	| Planning | Chart, the pick (CT-7, CT-9) | *Sober competence* (ART 2.11) | Shopping, routing software, a quest board |
105	| Mid-sortie pause | Panel over the frozen world (CT-3, CT-4) | *A held breath.* The world is paused in the middle of being itself | A safe room, a decompression chamber, a dimmed "you are safe now" scrim |
106	| Natural stop | Save & Quit (CT-21) | *Closing the log.* "Natural stop: the ship is stable again." (CON:184) | A reward, "progress saved!", an autosave flourish |
107	| Mid-crisis quit while DOWNED | Hold-to-confirm "quit without saving", "the newest autosave will be used" (SL UI-3) | *Plain honesty about the cost* | A death screen, "you died", a guilt line |
108	
109	### Anchor moments
110	
111	All four occur in the MVP slice (home-ship 5 / derelict A 4 / derelict B 5 compartments, LSG MVP slice; WM roster). Glyphs and colours are WM section 3 (WM:1036-1050) and ART 7.4, cited and not restated with new values.
112	
113	**Moment 1, "The table remembers what you lit" (first sortie; the Discovery payoff).** The cryo bay is stable. The player walks to the home pod console and presses with no pick. The console does not refuse: the chart opens (CT-10, "a press with no valid pick opens the chart"). Full-bleed Ground; concentric steps darkening inward (CT-13); one Tungsten point with a rectilinear Foundry silhouette for HOME; two plain Graphite-lit rectangles, bare, no labels, for derelicts A and B (UNSEEN, WM:1041; on the spatial map, which is the layout at every MVP canvas row at `H_default`, and in the compact layout only the CT-44 neutral ordinal appears, identical for UNSEEN and SEEN, a slot mark and not a name). Focus starts on HOME, not on a target, so focus is never a recommendation. The player snaps the bracket to A (CT-6); nothing appears beside it: no distance, no fuel, no name (CT-14, CT-35). Esc, resume, press. After the leg and the residual lamp (WM Moment 1), the next time the chart opens A is a Foundry silhouette with **one 1-art-px Tungsten tick** (WM:1043). *What the player learns:* the chart grows only by looking. It is a record of the crew's own eyes.
114	
115	**Moment 2, "Stopping the clock is not stopping the world" (solo pause mid-tell at low sanity; the P1 + P4 payoff).** In derelict B, sanity at stage 3, a scrubber gauge reads fixed while frost creeps along the floor (CON P4(b)). The 10-30 s tell has begun (P2). The player presses Esc. A short cut-fade (inside the ART 7.3 band) and the right-third panel is on Ground: Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit, in Paper White, the same at stage 3 as at stage 0 (CT-2, HR-6). To the left, the world is frozen **undimmed**: the lying gauge still reads fixed, the frost is still frost, the violet fringe on the gauge rim is still there, held in one frame (PIPE:265). Nothing on the panel says anything about any of it. Resume: the tell continues from exactly where it stopped. *What the player learns:* the menu is a place to stand, not a way out. It holds the world still; it does not make it kinder.
116	
117	**Moment 3, "The log, not the trophy" (next evening, the main menu; the P5 tone payoff).** Boot, main menu. Continue carries one line of SIM facts as words: playtime, crew count, kind, `RING 1` (SL UI-4 as amended: no `RISKY`; CT-23) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. No thumbnail, no screenshot of the ship, no "you were here", no percentage. If the newest record was unreadable, one plain ship-log line says so and Continue proceeds from the one before (SL UI-7). *What the player learns:* the game keeps a log of where they were, the way a ship does, and it will not flatter them.
118	
119	**Moment 4, "The ship is drawn from your history" (after the weld; the Fantasy / Investment payoff).** Derelict B was berthed and its sections welded. On the chart B first abuts the home silhouette with a solid 1-px Hull Grey seam (berthed, WM:1044), and once absorbed it is drawn **as part of the home silhouette**, no tick (WM:1045). The home mark is now a different shape from the one in Moment 1. Nothing announces it; there is no "ship expanded" banner. The drawing rule that makes this visible is the home-ship composite of CT-11 (the record's glyph at its authored `home_attach` point, seam drawn while berthed and erased once absorbed) and its reference captures (AC-CT-120) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *What the player learns:* "a ship that is literally assembled from your history" (CON:200, Retention: Investment) is visible on the one surface that cannot lie about it.
120	
121	**Moment-ordering tripwire.** A 30-minute MVP solo session (CON:483-485) reaches Moments 1 and 2 almost certainly, Moment 4 if the weld is reached, Moment 3 at the second launch. If playtest notes call the chart "empty" or "useless" before Moment 1's tick appears, the cure is **not** to add data to the chart; it is to check that the residual lamp and the tick are legible (WM, ART). Adding a label, cost or name is never one of the levers.
122	
123	### Design tests
124	
125	> **Primary (P1):** "A chart that tells you where to go and what it costs vs. a chart that only remembers what your crew lit → the one that remembers."
126	> **Secondary (pause, P1 + P2):** "A pause that softens the world vs. a pause that holds the world exactly as it was → the held world."
127	> **Tertiary (records, P5 + the no-win-state anti-pillar):** "A save screen that shows how far you have come vs. a log line that shows where you were → the log line."
128	
129	| Test | Rejects | Checkable as |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| Primary | fuel cost, travel time, ETA, distance label, danger/loot rating, "recommended", a name on an UNSEEN node, an interpolated pod marker, a route reconstructed from the pick | review against WM:1036-1050 and CT-35; lint on strings (CT-28); (auto) the chart double reads only `web.view` and never `web.leg_timing()` (CT-27) |
132	| Secondary | dim, blur, desaturation, vignette, scrim, slow-motion, a calming cue, a sanity-relief effect, any element that changes with sanity stage | screenshots at stage 0 and forced stage 3 (AC-SN-83); pixel diff of the world region before Esc and while the panel is up equals zero |
133	| Tertiary | thumbnail, completion %, "rings charted", achievement row, wall-clock nudge, "you died", "game over" | screenshot of UI-4; SL vocabulary lint (SL AC-SL-86) |
134	
135	Further tests this system adds, from the concept's own form: a **dimmed or blurred world behind the pause panel vs the world frozen exactly as lit → frozen**; a **death screen, "loading" indicator or tip vs black then control (ART 2.10, SL UI-6) → black**; a **minimap in play vs a chart you open (ART 7.0 "No minimap in play") → the chart you open**; a **confirm dialog on the hop vs the console press as the point of no return (WM:1225) → the press**.
136	
137	### Under hallucination: how the fantasy deepens, never breaks
138	
139	The layer has **no corruptible surface** (CT-2; PIPE PR-3/PR-10; PF:223; SN:1226). "Deepens" therefore cannot mean "the menu lies". It means three things, and the third is this system's one new rule.

content.content:
140	
141	1. **The contrast sharpens.** At stage 0 the panel and the world agree; at stage 3 the panel is the only thing on screen the player is sure of, and the world beside it is frozen mid-lie (Moment 2). The layer's value as an anchor rises exactly as the world's falls. Nothing on the layer changes for this to happen; the world changes around it. This is P4's "at least one channel of truth always remains", given a fixed place on screen (HR-6).
142	2. **The frozen lie is intended, and documented as intended.** `PAUSED_FROZEN` holds the last frame, including any hallucination, undimmed (PIPE:265). A tester or player at stage 3 will see a phantom held still beside a true menu. That image is the fantasy working, not a fault. It is an Edge Case and a QA note (Edge Cases, Acceptance Criteria), so nobody "fixes" it with a dim.
143	3. **Narrow truth (CT-39): the table is true, and it is not an oracle.** *The layer displays only facts that no hallucination class can lie about.* Every field it draws comes from `web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status` or `restore_reason`, and none of them is touched by classes (a), (b), (c) or (d). Conversely, **a fact that any hallucination class can falsify (Graph state, entity presence or position, salvage contents or value, a crewmate's rendered form or location) never enters the layer**, because a true copy of it on a free, pausable menu would make that lie free to disprove, and P4 requires that "checking costs time, risk or trust" (CON:263). This is the positive form of the negative rules CT-31 to CT-37 and gives the review one test instead of seven lists: *if a hallucination could make the world disagree with this field, the field does not belong here.*
144	
145	| Hallucination class | May it touch the Chart Table? | Why the fantasy holds |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| (a) phantom entities | Never. No entity, threat, proximity or "last seen" element exists on the layer (CT-32; HE:377, :1358) | the chart cannot confirm or deny a phantom, so checking one still costs a look into the dark |
148	| (b) false system states | Never. No Graph, module or suit datum exists on the layer (CT-34, CT-37; LSG:22 "never operates the Graph as a menu") | the scrubber that reads fixed must still be checked against the frost |
149	| (c) crewmates as horrors (VS-B) | Never wraps the layer. **Risk K1:** ART 7.4 / 7.5 reserve a crewmate beam-shape glyph on the chart as "one of exactly three ways to find a crewmate". Under OVERLAY that glyph is a zero-cost check against class (c) | the human channel is P1-inviolable, so the glyph is true; whether its *price* is right is VS-B's call (Open Questions) |
150	| (d) phantom salvage | Never. No loot value, contents or remaining-salvage count (CT-33; BS:334, AC-BS-47c) | the crate is still checked by weight, a second scanner or the trip home (CON P4(d)) |
151	
152	**Negatives lifted into rules:** no gleam, glide, tremor or settle on any element (ART 7.3: those signatures are readings only); no violet or flesh at any stage (ART 4.6, HR-6); no change of filament drift, ring darkness, font, scale or layout with sanity stage; no sanity-stage-dependent audio on the UI bus (AA:562).
153

155

findings.section: Adaptive Audio dependency / CT-18, CT-29, AC-CT-129
findings.finding: The Adaptive Audio row says the master-volume step contract is consistent (CT-29), but adaptive-audio-and-tells.md contains no VOLUME_STEPS, no step-to-gain law, no unity default, and no SettingsStore consumer. The only 'master' hits are the master identity table and the peak warning. ASK-CT-20 (the cue) was accepted as AAV-40, but the volume half of the D85 control was never raised as an ask, so the control publishes a step that nothing consumes.

Record the answer here and in AC-CT-129. Until then, mark the Adaptive Audio 'Consistent' cell 'Partly (volume half pending)'.

findings.section: States and Transitions TX-38 guard (L574)
findings.finding: The guard says 'PauseGate.can_save_quit is false because that refusal result arrived'. can_save_quit is defined as SOLO and kernel PAUSED (CT-4), so from PANEL or CHART in SOLO it is true. Read literally, TX-38 can never fire from an in-session state, and AC-CT-103b (layer open in SOLO, result SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED, expect UI3_PLATE) would fail. The table is data, diffed by AC-CT-93a, so the guard_id must be unambiguous.
findings.fix: Replace the guard with 'the window-close handler's save_and_quit() returned SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED' and drop the can_save_quit clause. State that TX-38 fires from CLOSED and from every in-session state except HOLD_CONFIRM and SAVE_QUIT_WAIT, regardless of can_save_quit.

findings.section: Edge Cases EC-CT-70 and header L15 vs R13/R14
findings.finding: EC-CT-70 says a reload 'reproduces rather than rerolls' because streams derive from the world seed and a state counter. R13/R14 make restore_epoch part of the draw key: a death-stub restore and a Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation (for example Quit-without-saving then Continue) advance the epoch, so threat draws deliberately differ. A Continue of a QUIT generation keeps the epoch. The header (L15) also claims 'R13/R14 do not touch this file', which this edge case contradicts.
findings.fix: Rewrite EC-CT-70: 'Save & Quit then Continue restores the same epoch and replays identically. Quit without saving then Continue restores an earlier generation with an advanced epoch (SL-23, R13/R14), so threat draws differ by design; no menu path lets the player choose or replay a favourable draw. The menu has no seed field.' Correct the L15 sentence.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S, C-10, AC-CT-127
findings.finding: DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S has a safe range of 0.3 to 0.8, the loader refuses only values above 0.8, and C-10 is 'cannot occur by construction'. At base 0.6 the margin is DELETE (min(1.2, 1.9) = 1.2) minus quit (0.6) = 0.6 s, whatever the cap. A margin above 0.6 therefore violates C-10 at the low end of the Controller's base range. The AC-CT-127 corner sweep would load 0.8 as valid and then fail C-10.
findings.fix: Narrow the range to 0.3-0.6 and have the loader refuse above 0.6 (equivalently, require margin <= min over bases of min(2b, 1.9) - min(b, cap)). Make CT_HOLD_CAP_S range 1.3-1.6 to match. Keep AC-CT-127's C-10 sweep as the check.

findings.section: CT-21 ceiling vs Save/Load; ASK-CT-7; TX-21; Gaps F-B
findings.finding: (a) CT-21, the Tuning 'cited' row and AC-CT-137(c) call 3,000 ms 'this layer's ceiling', but the owner's range is still 2,000-15,000, so a configured value can exceed the ceiling. Only the default is testable. (b) CT-21 and TX-21 depend on return values 'STARTED' and 'REFUSED_DOWNED'. Save/Load's API only names SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED and SL_QUIT_DEDUPED, so AC-CT-109's 'real result enum' check cannot match. ASK-CT-7 is still marked 'Open (new)'. (c) Gap F-B still lists ASK-CT-13 and ASK-CT-14 as 'still open', although both are answered.
findings.fix: Either ask Save/Load to narrow SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS to 2,000-3,000, or reword to 'the owner's default is 3,000 ms'. Define 'STARTED' as any result other than SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED (including SL_QUIT_DEDUPED) and 'REFUSED_DOWNED' as SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED. Close ASK-CT-7 on that mapping. Rewrite F-B so only ASK-CT-12b is open.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-137(b)
findings.finding: The criterion allows 'T_cfg plus at most one frame' from accept to FAILED. CT-21 requires one presented disabled frame before save_and_quit() is called, and Save/Load polls the timeout per frame (AC-SL-45c). A correct implementation measures T_cfg plus two frames from the accept (<= 3,000 + 34 ms), so the stated bound fails a correct build.
findings.fix: Measure from the call instant, or state the bound from the accept as 'T_cfg plus at most two frames (<= 3,000 + 34 ms at 60 fps at the owner's default)'.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-117, AC-CT-109(e)
findings.finding: Both criteria schema-check the Adapter double against 'AC-PCI-225 to 228'. The Controller's MenuInput criteria are AC-PCI-226 to 229, and the per-verb cap test is AC-PCI-230. findings.fix: Change both cites to 'AC-PCI-226 to 229' and cite AC-PCI-230 for the CT_HOLD_CAP_S contract in AC-CT-36(g) and AC-CT-127.

findings.section: Formulas D.9 / CT-45 / Tuning 'cited' row vs Player Controller
findings.finding: D.9 says an edge is 'released only below MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT'. CT-45 says 'MOVE_DEADZONE to take an edge, MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT to release it'. The owner (PCI L466, PC-2a(b), AC-PCI-227) defines MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT (0.05) as a band, so the release threshold is MOVE_DEADZONE minus MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT (0.20). Read literally, the CT wording releases at 0.05 and a stick would stay latched. The Adapter applies it, so no layer code is affected, but the unit is stated wrongly (R8).
findings.fix: Reword D.9, CT-45(2) and the cardinal-axis rule to 'released below MOVE_DEADZONE - MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT (the owner's exit band)'. Add the numeric example 0.25 / 0.05 / 0.20.

findings.section: S2 / EC-CT-31 / AC-CT-89 vs CT-21 and SL UI-2
findings.finding: The panel's FAILED word is keyed on bare 'save_status == FAILED' in S2, EC-CT-31 and AC-CT-89, but CT-21 says save_status is sticky across earlier autosave failures and that quit_held, 'not a stale FAILED', is the trigger. Save/Load UI-2 forbids a save fact on the pause panel; an autosave failure belongs to the HUD notice (UI-10). The panel could therefore show FAILED after a pure autosave failure with no quit attempted.
findings.fix: State once that the panel word is shown iff quit_held is true (the Save & Quit path failed or timed out), or a Retry plate is the entry. Restate S2, EC-CT-31, TX-23 and AC-CT-89 with the same condition, and add a case where an AUTO write fails and the panel stays empty.

findings.section: Edge Cases EC-CT-41; UI Requirements S14; EC-CT-13; AC-CT-9
findings.finding: Four leftovers from the third and fourth passes remain. (1) EC-CT-41 (L966) and S14 (L1537) list UI-9 as 'Quit, New campaign', against CT-25, CT-UI-5 and AC-CT-58 (New campaign first). (2) EC-CT-13 says whether the kernel coalesces is 'ASK-CT-9', which is answered. (3) AC-CT-9 says 'GIVEN any in-session depth, WHEN chart_table is pressed, THEN CLOSED' with no exemption for HOLD_CONFIRM (CT-5: abort only, no close) or SAVE_QUIT_WAIT (ignored). Extend CT-41(1) to 'opened by a console press, a governor release, or any boot transition'.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-84, AC-CT-81, AC-CT-37, AC-CT-25 (untestable as written)
findings.finding: AC-CT-84: 'the bracket reaches its new position over 100 ms with an ease-out, evidenced by a position table at t = 0, 50 and 100 ms' gives no expected values or tolerance. AC-CT-81 is BLOCKING but only 'reported against [PLACEHOLDER: 0.5 ms]', with no pass line (the 0.5 ms and the RM-DESKTOP/RM-DECK spike are intentional placeholders, but the criterion needs an assertion). findings.fix: AC-CT-84: 'with p(t) = p0 + (p1 - p0) * (1 - (1 - t/100)^2) rounded to whole HUD px (CT-GF-7(4)), the logged positions at t = 0, 50 and 100 ms equal p0, p0 + 0.75 * (p1 - p0) and p1 within 1 HUD px; at t >= 100 the position equals p1; under reduced motion the position is p1 on the first frame.' AC-CT-81: 'p95 script time <= 0.5 ms [PLACEHOLDER] on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; the criterion fails above it'. AC-CT-37: 'the 50 % capture matches the retained golden within zero pixels on the pinned runner; the needle protrudes >= 1 art px above and below the bar; the fill and the bar interior differ by >= 3:1 relative luminance (AC-CT-75c GLYPH)'. findings.section: Dependencies / Cross-References vs Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline; AC-CT-45; D.10
findings.finding: (a) AC-CT-45 and D.10 assert that layer 2 is not drawn under a full-bleed plate. The Pipeline has no such rule, ASK-CT-12b is still open, and pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md row 7 still says 'three display controls' (CT-18 now has four, with master volume). findings.finding: The guard says 'PauseGate.can_save_quit is false because that refusal result arrived'. can_save_quit is defined as SOLO and kernel PAUSED (CT-4), so from PANEL or CHART in SOLO it is true.
